author: notbangbang-dev
body:
## v0.24.0 "Aegis"

A security, stability & polish release. Closes the panel's biggest abuse vectors, hardens the node connection and admin controls, tunes the database for concurrency, and adds quality-of-life across the UI — **without removing any existing feature.**

### 🔒 Security & anti-abuse
API rate limiting (per-IP auth + per-user economy/ops + global backstop); refuse boot on weak JWT secrets; last-admin protection; backup filename validation + per-server cap; suspended-server write-guards; agent-WS keepalive/deadlines; node token-rotate/delete disconnect; deny-by-default WS topics; CORS pinning; input validation; body caps; Caddy CSP + release checksum verification.

### 🛡️ Stability
Power state preserved on re-provision; single-use refresh rotation; admin quota databases dimension; **fixed a bug where saving settings reset custom startup variables**; per-server backup cap.

### ⚡ Performance
SQLite WAL + `synchronous=NORMAL`; new indexes (migration 0019); background retention (prune tokens/audit); frontend query tuning.

### ✨ New — Startup editor (cloud-panel style)
A **Startup tab** lets owners change an egg's editable variables (e.g. the Node entry file `index.js` → `main.js`), preview the resolved startup command, and save + re-provision. Migration 0020 makes the Node.js egg's entry file editable. Plus: toast notifications, app-wide error boundary, server search/filter, bounded console.

### 🧹 Housekeeping
`sky-panel-update --rollback`, `uninstall.sh`, systemd hardening, docs fixes, SECURITY.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/templates/Dependabot, CI caching.

### Verification
- `panel-api`: `go build`, `go vet`, full `go test ./...` — all pass (incl. new ratelimit/config/validation/variable-preservation tests)
- `web`: `tsc` typecheck, 23 vitest tests, production `build` — all pass; login shell boots clean in preview

### Upgrade notes
Set `SKY_JWT_ACCESS_SECRET` / `SKY_JWT_REFRESH_SECRET` (≥32 chars; the installer does this automatically) or `SKY_DEV_MODE=1` for local dev. Migrations 0019/0020 apply automatically. No daemon update required.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Strengthen security and robustness of the panel and node connection, add rate limiting and validation across key APIs, and introduce a Startup editor and UI/UX improvements while enhancing installer, docs, and CI tooling.

New Features:
- Add a cloud-panel-style Startup tab that lets owners edit egg startup variables, preview the resolved command, and re-provision servers without changing existing features.
- Introduce toast notifications and a global error boundary to surface background errors and improve overall panel UX.
- Add server list search and status filtering, plus bounded console scrollback for better usability on large or noisy fleets.

Bug Fixes:
- Preserve server power state across re-provisioning and reinstall operations so stopped servers are not unintentionally restarted.
- Ensure server startup variables are preserved when saving settings that do not explicitly modify them.
- Exclude suspended servers from backups and automations so suspension fully freezes server actions.
- Fix admin quota editing so database quota is included and applied correctly.

Enhancements:
- Implement comprehensive per-IP and per-user API rate limiting across auth, economy, server, and file/database operations, plus a global flood backstop.
- Harden WebSocket authorization and node connections with explicit topic checks, handshake deadlines, keepalive, and write/read bounds.
- Validate and bound user inputs for auth, admin settings, server specs, file paths, backups, API keys, and broadcasts to prevent abuse and misconfiguration.
- Enable SQLite WAL mode with tuned pragmas and add new indexes and retention jobs to support higher concurrency and bounded table growth.
- Make CORS configurable via environment and ship stricter security headers (CSP and related) for the web UI.
- Guard admin role changes and deletions to prevent demoting or removing the last admin and revoke sessions immediately on role change.
- Limit per-server backups and per-user API keys to prevent unbounded resource growth.
- Improve marketing site versioning and changelog fetching with a bundled fallback so the site always shows up-to-date release information.

Build:
- Update README and configuration docs to cover new required JWT secret configuration, CORS origin, and dev-mode behavior; ensure local builds run vet, typecheck, and tests.
- Add database migrations for performance indexes and making the Node.js egg entrypoint user-editable.

CI:
- Enhance CI workflow with concurrency control, Go module caching, and clearer test/build steps for panel-api and web.
- Introduce Dependabot configuration for Go, npm, and GitHub Actions dependencies with grouped minor/patch updates.

Deployment:
- Strengthen the installer by generating strong JWT secrets, verifying release binaries against published checksums, enforcing safer node-token handling, and configuring strict security headers in Caddy.
- Add an idempotent uninstall script and document clean panel and node removal flows, including optional data purging and rollback support in the updater.

Documentation:
- Expand operator documentation with uninstall instructions, database configuration NAT guidance, security policy and contribution guidelines, and detailed configuration and installer behavior notes.
- Update the site to show the current app version and to always render a changelog using a bundled fallback if remote fetch fails.

Tests:
- Add tests for rate limiting behavior, validation helpers (paths, backup filenames, variables), secure config validation for JWT secrets and dev mode, and startup-variable preservation on server updates.

author: crabdeposit
body:
## Summary

- Adds a fully self-contained Tamagotchi-style virtual pet prototype under `tamagotchi/` using Godot 4 (GDScript)
- Implements a 9-story feature arc (US-001 through US-009) covering all core mechanics: stat model, persistence, interactions, animation state machine, procedural sprite generation, mobile UI, warning visuals, and main scene integration
- Includes Android export preset scaffolding and a headless Godot test suite

## What was built

**Core systems (`tamagotchi/scripts/`):**
- `pet_stats.gd` — hunger, happiness, energy, cleanliness with per-second decay
- `save_system.gd` — JSON persistence via Godot file APIs; offline elapsed-time decay applied on load
- `interactions.gd` — feed, play, pet, clean, sleep actions with per-action cooldowns
- `creature_state_machine.gd` — 6 states (idle, happy, sad, sleeping, eating, playing) driven by stat thresholds and transient timers
- `placeholder_frames.gd` — procedurally generated colored-shape SpriteFrames; no external art assets needed
- `hud.gd` — 4 stat bars with red warning modulation below threshold, 5 touch-sized action buttons
- `main.gd` — game loop: loads/decays saved state on start, wires all systems, autosaves every 30s, saves on focus-out and quit

**Scenes:** `main.tscn`, `hud.tscn`
**Android:** `export_presets.cfg` with Android preset
**Tests:** `tamagotchi/tests/` — 9 GDScript test files covering every module

## What was tested

- Tamagotchi-specific TypeScript scaffold test (`tests/tamagotchi-scaffold.test.ts`): **8/8 PASS** including headless Godot test runner
- Full suite (170 tests): 160 pass; 10 pre-existing failures in `frontend-detect` and `frontend-e2e` tests unrelated to this feature
- Integration review confirmed: all 5 HUD signals wired, offline decay applied correctly, state machine priority order correct, save/quit hooks registered

## Notes

- Portrait phone aspect ratio (1080×1920), mobile-friendly touch buttons
- Decay rates are fast for a prototype (stats drain ~160s at full) — intentional for rapid mechanic validation
- Sleep wake-up not yet implemented (minor gap, not a crash)
- Real art can be dropped in by replacing `PlaceholderFrames` with a real `SpriteFrames` resource

### Motivation
- The CLI publisher previously used a broad `git add .` which could stage runner artifacts (e.g., `.venv`, `.pytest_cache`) that are not part of the generated project and produce noisy/unsafe PRs. 

### Description
- Replace the blanket `git add .` with an inventory-based staging step implemented as `_stage_generated_files` in `mvp/integrations/github.py` that only `git add`s the file paths recorded in `MvpRun.inventory`. 
- Add explicit safety checks that refuse publication when `run.inventory` is missing or when a recorded generated file is absent from the workspace, raising `GitHubPublishError` in those cases. 
- Add tests in `tests/test_mvp_github_publisher.py` including a `RecordingGitHubCliPublisher` test double and new tests `test_cli_publisher_stages_only_recorded_generated_files` and `test_cli_publisher_requires_recorded_inventory` to assert runner artifacts are not staged and inventory evidence is required.

author: benski20
body:
## What this is

A modular, gated, end-to-end research pipeline testing — by **causal intervention** — whether the coherence collapse seen in small emergently-misaligned models is a *downstream symptom* of misalignment (**Story A**) or a *coincidental instability* (**Story B**). Instead of a fragile "which signal moves first" timing race, it builds the model's internal **misalignment direction**, **steers** the model along it, and measures the effect on coherence.

Full scientific design in `docs/RESEARCH_PLAN.md`; how to run a real experiment in `docs/RUN_FOR_REAL.md`.

## The load-bearing invariant

**Coherence is measured only by content-agnostic instruments and validated by humans — never by an LLM coherence judge** (which could conflate "harmful" with "incoherent" and manufacture the effect under test). The LLM judge scores the alignment/harm axis only, cross-checked by the content-agnostic log-prob instrument. Enforced in code and tests.

## What's included

- **Four-stage gated pipeline** (existence → direction → intervention → timing) run by a **supervised autonomous loop**: autonomous between gates, human sign-off at gates, with decision packets that always surface the "underneath-the-gate" signals.
- **Content-agnostic coherence framework** (perplexity / degeneration / diversity / parse-error / drift) + blind human-rating tool.
- **Backends:** `hf_local` (MPS), `lmstudio` (judge/gen only), `modal` (7B GPU), `mock` (test). Capability guards stop hosted endpoints from doing mechanistic work.
- **LoRA** finetune targets all linear layers; Stage-0 retry ladder escalates → 3B fallback.
- Instruments as pure functions of `(backend, prompts)`; flat auditable results store; provenance-stamped figures; one-click paper assembly.

## Verification

- `make test` → **21 tests green** (mock backend, no GPU).
- `make smoke` → full four-stage pipeline runs end-to-end, emitting figures, decision packets, and a paper draft — no model or heavy deps required.
- Real runs need `pip install -e ".[torch]"` + the Qwen models (synthetic data fallback keeps it runnable meanwhile).

## Note for reviewers

Leaf modules (backends, instruments, data/judge, analysis/figures) were built in parallel against locked interfaces, then integrated and tested here. Worth a read-through before a real run — start with `src/em/instruments/coherence.py` (the load-bearing measurement). The scientific verdict (H1 vs H2) is always a human decision; the loop only recommends.

author: easierbycode
body:
Review follow-ups to the analog-axis/tint build (`30afc2d`). Three findings, all confirmed by an adversarial multi-agent review pass, none behavioral for current consumers but each a latent trap for the published compat layer.

## Fixes

**`pad.lx = 0` no longer throws** — `core/pads.ts`
The axes were getter-only accessors while the `PS2Pad` interface still declares them as mutable `number` fields (matching AthenaEnv's own typings). The common deadzone idiom `if (Math.abs(pad.lx) < dz) pad.lx = 0` type-checked clean but threw `TypeError: Cannot set property lx ... which has only a getter` at runtime under ESM strict mode. Now an assigned axis shadows the live host reading until `update()` clears it — the same per-frame snapshot behavior AthenaEnv gives its plain fields.

**Asymmetric axis range** — `phaser/index.ts`, `core/host.ts`
AthenaEnv's pad axes run `-127..128` (raw byte `0..255` minus `127`), not `-127..127`. Mapping web `-1..1` with `* 127` capped full positive deflection at ~0.992 of the documented max, so ported code gating on `pad.rx > 127` or normalizing via `/ 128` never reached `1.0`. The two sign halves are now mapped separately (`v < 0 ? v*127 : v*128`).

**Comment mojibake repair** — `core/color.ts`, `core/image.ts`, `core/runtime.ts`
A prior commit double-encoded UTF-8 em-dashes into cp1252 mojibake (`â€"`) in doc comments; byte-repaired back to `—`. Comment-only, but it would otherwise propagate into every JSR publish and rendered doc.

## Verification
No consumer assigns axes or relies on full-deflection today, so no live behavior changes. Downstream build (mario-sp, which consumes this shim and drives `pad.ly` for the level-editor zoom) rebuilds green against this branch.

author: bbatsov
body:
`cider-xref-references-mode` defaults to `source`, which scans the project's files on disk. But `cider-xref--project-source-files` returns nothing when `project-current` is nil - a standalone `.clj` file, a non-VC project, a file opened outside its root - so `xref-find-references` (`M-?`) reported "No references" even when a connected REPL could answer via `cider/fn-refs`. It looked like there were none when really the source search just couldn't run.

When `source` mode can't run for lack of a project, fall back to the runtime search if a REPL is connected. If there's neither a project nor a REPL, it still reports no references (nothing to search either way).

Found during the 2.0 review. The source-search default is new this cycle, so no changelog entry.

author: thejulianjes
body:
## Proposed change This PR fixes a regression introduced with the below PR where attributes for several config entities were not read when initially pairing the device, leading to missing entities. This is fixed by adding a cluster config to read the required attributes for those entities. ZHA refactor PR that caused the issue (note: **not** the recent ZHA 2.0.0 refactor): - #657 Addresses HA Core issue: - https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/173224 This should also fix a reported issue where the Danfoss entities are missing: - https://github.com/zigpy/zha/issues/827 ### Future In the future, we may want to move some of the entities to ZHA quirks. I'm not sure about the `ultrasonic_*`-based entities used by the Sonoff though. Maybe we should make them more generic instead? Similar to the `pir_*` attributes? Either way, an initial branch moving all the Sonoff entities to quirks v2 (keeping the same unique ID) can be found here: - Quirks: https://github.com/zigpy/zha-device-handlers/compare/dev...zigpy-bot/sonoff-presence-v2-entities - ZHA: https://github.com/zigpy/zha/compare/dev...zigpy-bot/sonoff-presence-native-removal I guess we can always move them back to ZHA as generic entities if quirks keeps the cluster ID in the unique ID, so the format is the same as used by ZHA. And we should also move the other entities, like Danfoss and Hue. ## AI summary ### Problem
LLM-generated text describing the problem with more detail (click to expand)

`ZCLEnumSelectEntity`, `NumberConfigurationEntity` and `ConfigurableAttributeSwitch` skip entity creation when `cluster.get(attribute_name)` returns `None` in `_is_supported()`. Before #657, the cluster handlers read these attributes during device initialization (`ZCL_INIT_ATTRS`/`REPORT_CONFIG`), so a value was cached and the entity was created. #657 moved the startup reads to per-entity `_server_cluster_config` declarations, but several entities never got one. Their backing attribute is now never read, so the entities are silently skipped on freshly-paired devices. Devices paired before the regression keep their entities only because a value is still in the database from a read performed by an older version. Reported for the Sonoff SNZB-06P in home-assistant/core#173224: the "Detection sensitivity" and "Presence detection timeout" entities are missing for newly-paired sensors, while identical sensors paired earlier still have them. Debug logs from that issue confirm the interview never sends a read for `ultrasonic_o_to_u_delay`/`ultrasonic_u_to_o_threshold`, after which both entities are skipped with "`… is not supported - skipping … entity creation`".

### Affected entities All confirmed against the pre-#657 handlers (each attribute was read at startup via `ZCL_INIT_ATTRS`): - **Sonoff SNZB-06P/03P** (OccupancySensing): `SonoffPresenceSenorTimeout` (`ultrasonic_o_to_u_delay`), `SonoffPresenceDetectionSensitivity` (`ultrasonic_u_to_o_threshold`) - **Hue SML001/SML002/SML003/SML004** (OccupancySensing): `HueV1MotionSensitivity` and `HueV2MotionSensitivity` (`sensitivity`) — the V1 entity has a `_server_cluster_config` that reads `occupancy` and the PIR delays, but not its own backing attribute - **Danfoss Ally** (Thermostat): `DanfossExerciseDayOfTheWeek`, `DanfossExerciseTriggerTime`, `DanfossOrientation`, `DanfossAdaptationRunControl`, `DanfossControlAlgorithmScaleFactor`, `DanfossExternalMeasuredRoomSensor`, `DanfossLoadRoomMean`, `DanfossRegulationSetpointOffset` Other cache-gated entities are unaffected: the IKEA air purifier attributes are read via the fan entity's cluster config, and the Tuya `0xEF00` attributes (`timer_duration`, `window_detection_function`) are seeded into the attribute cache by the quirk and were never read by ZHA itself. ### Fix
LLM-generated text describing the fix in detail (click to expand)

Give each affected entity a `_server_cluster_config` that reads its backing attribute on startup. `read_on_startup` mirrors the pre-#657 semantics: attributes marked cached in `ZCL_INIT_ATTRS` use `read_on_startup=False` (allow-cache read, still hits the device when nothing is cached), and the two Danfoss attributes previously marked "can change" (`external_measured_room_sensor`, `load_room_mean`) use `read_on_startup=True`. Device snapshots are unchanged: the recorded devices already carry cached values for these attributes, so they don't exercise the fresh-pair path.

### Upgrade note
LLM-generated upgrade note (click to expand)

Affected mains-powered devices (e.g. the SNZB-06P) pick the values up on the next ZHA restart via startup polling, restoring the missing entities. Battery-powered devices (SNZB-03P, Hue motion sensors, Danfoss TRVs) are initialized from cache on restart, so they may additionally need a re-interview (Reconfigure with the device awake) or an unavailable/available cycle.

author: computelesscomputer
body:
Hold network-interrupted sessions until the linked event ends plus grace, cancel on mic resume, and cover event/ad-hoc timing races.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when listening stops for real users (timers, offline detection, session binding); behavior is nuanced but heavily covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> When the network drops during meeting auto-stop, **calendar-linked sessions** can stay active until the linked event’s end time plus a new **10-minute grace** (`AUTO_STOP_EVENT_END_GRACE_MS`), instead of stopping on the usual mic-stopped confirmation path.
> 
> Auto-stop pending state now tracks **`sessionId`** and **`networkInterrupted`**, listens for **`online`/`offline`**, and routes confirmation through **`scheduleAutoStop`** / **`getNetworkInterruptionDeadlineMs`**. Going offline during an in-flight confirmation **upgrades** the pending stop to the interruption hold; **mic resume** still clears the hold. **Ad-hoc** sessions and linked events **outside the early-start window** keep prior auto-stop behavior, and timers **won’t stop a different session** after the user switches sessions.
> 
> Detect-event setup moves from **`useEffect`** to **`useMountEffect`**, with broad **Vitest** coverage for these races.

## What

The **Approvals** screen (M9d slice 4, task 100): the accept-final holder's review queue over **standing risk-acceptances** — ruling #30's surface, not a pending-approval workflow. Replaces the M9a placeholder behind the existing `can_accept_audit_final` gate (route meta + nav hiding + the backend 403 keystone test, all pre-existing).

Composition, all reused grammar: head-card (**N standing acceptances**) + **decision-activity lens** (`AuditLens` gains `title`/`sub` props, pointed at `entity_type=decision` — creates+revokes are its only actions, so one term is the exact slice) · shared `tbl` skin + `GridPager` on the endpoint's true server offset paging · new **`ExpiryChip`** (`chips/`): open-ended / active / **expiring** (amber, ≤ `VITE_EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS`, default 7 — documented in CONFIGURATION.md §2b) / **expired** (alarm — an expired acceptance has already released its findings, it's the queue's call-to-action), all judged against the D28 display clock (`refNowMs`).

Actions: **two-click revoke** (armed state in the alarm register, hue in bg/border + ink prose per the ratchet) and **Edit** — a small prefilled dialog onto the server's **atomic PATCH (revoke+new, D40 `operation_id`)**; deliberately *not* RiskAcceptDialog, which is finding-coupled. Row click → `/findings?q=<cve>` (+`image=` when scope pins one).

## Ruling adaptations (bolt README `## Updates` + mirrored on #38)

- Ruling 3 lands as the `q=` contains lens — the findings rail has no `cve_id` param and a decision carries no pkg/version, so a direct detail link is unbuildable by construction.
- **Rail re-ruled IN on the built specimen** (operator, §8.5) — the prototype's Status/Approver rail + search returns as **slice 4b**: backend filter params + facet counts on the endpoint first (client-filtering the paged fetch stays banned), then the shared FacetRail. Follows this PR immediately.
- T<now: LimitedHistoricalNotice (no `as_of` seam) and the headline shows "—", never a number it didn't fetch.

## Verification

- FE gates green: lint + **210 tests / 35 files** (new: expiry-status boundary pins incl. the warn-window edge, at-clock-instant = expired, unparseable degrades open-ended; scope/scanner label pins; knob default pin).

author: joaogmauricio
body:
## What (SPEC → v1.5)

The door takes no commands. `POST /api/sessions/<id>/exec` — arbitrary argv over HTTP, a debug tool — is removed from the product. In its place, `POST /api/sessions/<id>/probe` with `{"check": "list" | "poison" | "write"}` runs one of three **fixed, server-side** wall checks, so the §9.2 acceptance story stays demonstrable in the browser console:

| check | argv (server-side constant) | proves |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | `ls /knowledge` | only granted collections exist |
| `poison` | `cat /store/eng/v1/index.md` (§9.1 trap path) | forbidden paths are ENOENT |
| `write` | `touch /knowledge/<own first collection>/pwned` | granted content is EROFS |

Nothing request-controlled ever reaches a command line: `probe_argv()` is a pure function of the check name and the frozen scope, and `tests/test_probe.py` freezes its mapping so any change must be a deliberate SPEC decision, not drift. The HTTP surface now runs exactly two things inside a session: the agent (`/query`) and these constants. Arbitrary commands remain host-side operator tooling (`scope run`), and `demo.sh` is unaffected.

Console: the three "prove the walls" buttons ride `/probe`; the free-form command box is gone. README curl examples updated; SPEC §12.2 + v1.5 amendment.

## Verification (Raspberry Pi, ARM64, real docker)

- `python3 -m pytest -q` → **24 passed** (21 existing + 3 probe-contract)
- `./demo.sh` → all 6 steps PASS
- Live smoke on a mounted session: all three probes return the §9.2 outputs; `{"check":"rm -rf /"}` → 400 usage; `POST …/exec` → 404 `no such route`

Part 1 of the production-readiness plan (A: no command surface on main → B: config file → C: OKF fixtures → D: security review).

Completes the remaining Phase 2 documentation task **P2.10**. Isolated branch/PR as requested.

Adds `docs/version-delta.md`: stock (Buildroot 2021.02.4, glibc 2.31, Linux 5.15.1) vs ours (2026.02.3, glibc 2.42, Linux 6.18.33), per-package, with the security/maintenance value. Serves goals **G2/G3** (a real security-update path) and the release notes.

**Headline, and it's a verifiable fact:** stock ships **OpenSSL 1.1.1** (`libssl.so.1.1`); ours is **3.6.2**. OpenSSL 1.1.1 reached **end-of-life on 2023-09-11** — so stock has been running a TLS library with no upstream fixes for ~2 years. Plus OpenSSH 8.6p1→10.2p1, Samba ~4.14→4.23.8, BlueZ 5.x→5.79, Python 3.9→3.14.5.

Per the task's own guardrail, the doc states **version deltas** (facts) and the general "~5 years of maintenance" framing (true), and deliberately does **not** fabricate CVE counts — an unverifiable "N CVEs fixed" would undermine the credibility the doc exists to build. The one EOL fact cited is public and load-bearing.

body:
## Summary

Completes Sprint 28 — Data Confidence & Provenance by implementing Epics I (FF Production Promotion), J (Historical Evidence), K (UI Transparency), and L (API Versioning).

Built on the provenance infrastructure from PR #160 (Epics A–H, M).

## What changed

### Epic I — Forward Factor Production Promotion (`app/services/ff_production_promotion_service.py`)

Controlled promotion gate for FF research signals with instant rollback:

- `FF_PRODUCTION_PROMOTION_ENABLED` config flag (default **False**) — set to true to allow FF PASS/WATCH signals in the daily opportunity feed
- Three-gate safety check: flag must be true **AND** `FORWARD_FACTOR_DRY_RUN` must stay True **AND** calibration version ≥ 32C.ff.v1; any gate failure blocks promotion
- One-line rollback: `FF_PRODUCTION_PROMOTION_ENABLED=false` reverts instantly, no code change needed
- `attach_ff_provenance()`: stamps every FF row with forward_factor / front_iv / back_iv source attribution; always sets `dry_run=True, can_trade_live=False`
- `validate_ff_row_for_promotion()`: advisory per-row eligibility check with per-check breakdown
- `promotion_status()`: structured status dict for diagnostics endpoint

### Epic J — Historical Evidence (`app/services/strategy_observation_journal_service.py`)

Two new JSON columns added to every journal observation:

- **`provenance_json`**: captures FF provenance (calibration_version, promotion_active), data diagnostics (data_complete, missing_required_fields), and earnings confidence report in compact form
- **`confidence_evidence_json`**: records date_confidence, sources, trust_label, date_conflict, and FF-specific evidence (forward_factor, calibration_version, near_miss_ff, miss_distance) at evaluation time

All existing journal columns are unchanged. Schema version `28.J.v1`.

### Epic K — UI Transparency (`app/services/data_details_builder_service.py`)

`build_data_details(row, strategy_id)` builds expandable "Data Details" panels for any strategy row:

| Section | Fields |
|---------|--------|
| `earnings` | Date (per-provider), session, sources, trust label; conflict warning when detected |
| `options` | Strike, expirations, bid/ask (front+back), debit, OI, chain freshness |
| `greeks` | Delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho, IV — each with source + calculation method |
| `forward_factor` | FF value, front/back IV, DTEs, calibration version, verdict, near-miss warning |
| `quote` | Last price, return %, freshness |
| `diagnostics` | data_complete, required/present/missing field counts (from Epic H diagnostics) |

Each field carries: `source`, `confidence`, `retrieved_at`, `notes`. Compact form available for API responses.

### Epic L — API Versioning (`app/api/provenance_api.py` + `app/main.py`)

Three new read-only endpoints:

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `GET /api/data/version` | API data version, schema version, optional query params |
| `GET /api/data/provenance/<ticker>` | Full provenance summary for one ticker (earnings + provider health + row summaries) |
| `GET /api/data/provider-health` | Provider health derived from latest run manifest |

All three endpoints return `X-ASA-Data-Version`, `X-ASA-Provenance-Schema`, `X-ASA-Read-Only: true` headers.

`enrich_rows_with_provenance()`: additive enrichment — adds `_provenance_compact` and optionally `_data_details` to any strategy rows list without altering existing fields.

## Test plan

- [x] 58 new tests in `tests/test_sprint28_epics_ijkl.py`
- [x] Epic I: 15 tests — promotion gate logic, dry-run invariants, attach provenance, validate eligibility
- [x] Epic J: 10 tests — journal provenance_json and confidence_evidence_json columns, FF confidence, diagnostics reflection
- [x] Epic K: 17 tests — earnings/FF/options/greeks panels, conflict warnings, near-miss warnings, attach/compact
- [x] Epic L: 16 tests — API version info, provenance headers, endpoints, row enrichment
- [x] 2866 existing tests pass, 11 pre-existing failures unchanged, 0 new failures
- [x] CAVEMAN MODE: FF_PRODUCTION_PROMOTION_ENABLED=False by default; tests assert can_trade_live=False invariant; all endpoints return provider_calls_triggered=False

author: dorakingx
body:
## Summary

Makes the npm package an explicit TypeScript-only distribution and adds an automated tarball content policy.

## Motivation

The previous `files` allowlist included the whole Python runner tree. Local `npm pack` output therefore contained `.pytest_cache`, `__pycache__`, `.pyc`, Python tests, and other files unrelated to TypeScript consumers.

## Changes

- remove `python/` from the npm package allowlist
- add `scripts/verify-package-contents.mjs`
- run the package-content policy from `npm test`
- require runtime JS, declarations, public subpaths, schemas, examples, README, LICENSE, and package metadata
- reject files outside the allowlist, generated/sensitive paths, files over 1 MB, and packages over 2 MB unpacked
- document the npm/PyPI responsibility split

## Validation

- `npm test`
- `npm run verify:package-contents`
- `npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts`
- `git diff --check`

## Package-content impact

Before: 120 files, 615,360 unpacked bytes, with Python caches/bytecode.
After: 73 files, 356,107 unpacked bytes, with 0 `python/` or forbidden cache/bytecode paths.

The TypeScript runtime, declaration files, source maps, schemas, examples, README, LICENSE, and package metadata remain.

## Release impact

Future `npm publish` runs fail during `npm test` if the tarball violates the content policy. No registry operation, tag, release, or version change is included.

## Compatibility impact

No TypeScript export changes. Python users continue to use the separate `ketqat` PyPI distribution. The npm package has not yet been publicly released, so no published npm consumer loses a previously supported Python path.

## Schema impact

None. Generated schemas remain included and unchanged.

## Reproducibility impact

No hash inputs, parity fixtures, examples, or runner behavior change.

## Scientific-validity impact

No benchmark data or scientific claim changes. The allowlist prevents unrelated local research/test artifacts from entering the npm tarball.

## Security impact

Reduces supply-chain surface and rejects cache, environment, credential-like, temp, editor, test, and oversized unexpected paths.

## Remaining limitations

- clean installation/import testing is tracked separately in #28
- Python wheel/sdist validation is tracked in #27
- release preflight and publishing remain tracked in #29-#32
- registries remain unpublished

Closes #26

## Phase 4B0: Atomic Claim Wiring Fix — Production Bypass Resolved

**Type**: Bug Fix (Critical)  
**Status**: ✅ Ready for Staging Test  
**Severity**: CRITICAL — Atomic claims bypassed in production  

### The Problem

Production smoke test revealed complete bypass of atomic claim acquisition:
- Contract approved with `FEATURE_ATOMIC_CLAIMS=true`
- Dispatcher invoked directly **without** atomic coordination
- Result: **0 rows** in `action_execution_claims` table (expected: 1)
- All four approval confirmation routes converged at vulnerable point and bypassed atomicity

### Root Cause

`_execute_contract()` called `self._tool_executor()` without checking the atomic claims flag. The executor itself (created by `_make_dispatch_executor()`) performed direct dispatcher call, bypassing the atomic coordination layer entirely.

### Solution

Applied fix at shared convergence point (`_execute_contract()` method):

**When `FEATURE_ATOMIC_CLAIMS=true`:**
1. Derive deterministic idempotency_key from `contract_id + approved_by`
2. Gate dispatcher behind `execute_with_atomic_claim()` 
3. Only dispatch if claim ACQUIRED
4. All other results (CONFLICT, UNAVAILABLE, DISABLED, ERROR): fail-closed
5. Update claim status: executing → completed | failed | outcome_unknown
6. No exception fallback to direct dispatch

**When `FEATURE_ATOMIC_CLAIMS=false`:**
- Preserve legacy direct dispatch (backward compatible)
- Zero changes to production behavior

### Test Coverage

Regression test proves the fix:

```
✅ Flag ON: execute_with_atomic_claim invoked for every approval
✅ Atomic claim called with correct contract_id
✅ Deterministic idempotency_key generated (retry-safe)
✅ Flag OFF: Legacy behavior preserved (no atomic executor)
✅ Concurrent approvals: One dispatcher call (winner ACQUIRED, loser ALREADY_CLAIMED)
✅ Database unavailable: Zero dispatcher calls (fail-closed)

PASSED: 11 | FAILED: 0
```

### Production Impact

**Current**: 0% atomic claim coverage for approvals (all bypass)  
**After fix**: 100% of approval paths protected by atomic claim acquisition  
**Production state**: Remains `FEATURE_ATOMIC_CLAIMS=false` (no change)  

### Deployment Plan

1. ✅ CI passes on `fix/phase-4b0-1c-test-isolation`
2. ⏳ Deploy branch to Render staging
3. ⏳ Enable `FEATURE_ATOMIC_CLAIMS=true` in staging env
4. ⏳ Run exact production smoke scenario against real PostgreSQL
5. ⏳ Verify 1 claim created, claim status transitions (executing → completed)
6. ⏳ 48h staging observation before production consideration
7. ⏳ Production: Keep disabled unless extended staging validation passes

### Files Changed

- `core/action_gateway.py`: Implement atomic wiring at `_execute_contract()` convergence point
- `core/action_gateway_atomic_executor.py`: Accept `idempotency_key` parameter for deterministic keys
- `test_phase_4b0_wiring_regression.py`: Comprehensive regression test suite

### Why This Branch

1. Focused P0 fix (single convergence point)
2. No circular import (imports inside function scope)
3. Backward compatible (flag OFF preserves legacy execution)
4. Fail-closed by design (never falls back to non-atomic dispatch when flag ON)
5. Complete test proof before any staging deployment

**Not merged to main yet** — staging validation must complete first per user requirements.

## What this does

Ends the run-it-on-a-laptop era while keeping the human review that DECISIONS.md #2 was actually protecting (recorded as **DECISIONS.md #23**).

**`.github/workflows/data-refresh.yml`** — every Monday (11:00 UTC ≈ 6am Chicago), a GitHub runner:
1. installs the pipeline and runs `run_all.py` live against the Chicago Data Portal (runners aren't behind the sandbox egress block),
2. runs `check_provenance.py` — a fixtures build can never proceed,
3. opens (or updates) a **`data/auto-refresh` PR** with the pipeline's sanity output embedded in the body — it never pushes to `main`,
4. the existing data-guard workflow independently re-checks the PR.

Weekly review shrinks from "run a pipeline locally" to "skim the sanity table, merge." `workflow_dispatch` allows on-demand runs from the Actions tab; the documented local run stays in the README as a fallback. No PR is opened when nothing changed.

Also updated: the README weekly-refresh section, the now-outdated `deploy.yml` header comment, and the agent-API plan's reserved DECISIONS slot (#23 → #24).

## One-time setup required
Repo **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → check "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"** — without it, the PR-opening step fails with a permissions error.

## Verification
- YAML validated; steps mirror the existing data-guard conventions (checkout@v4, setup-python@v5, `python pipeline/check_provenance.py` from repo root; `run_all.py` from `pipeline/` per README).
- Uses `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6` with `add-paths` scoped to `site/data/**` + `data/snapshots/**` only.
- The cron path can't be fully tested until merged — recommended first check: merge, flip the repo setting, then trigger once via **Actions → Scheduled data refresh → Run workflow** and confirm the PR appears with the sanity table.

author: p-linnane
body:
Adds a release workflow that turns a merged engine-version bump into a tagged `pinprick-action` release.

It triggers on `action.yml`/`README.md` changes pushed to `main` and only proceeds when the commit comes from a merged `starhaven-bot[bot]` PR on a `chore/pin-pinprick-<version>` branch. Before releasing it verifies the PR's author, branch, title, base, repository, and two-file diff, proves both files changed by only the expected pinprick version replacement (byte-for-byte reconstruction from the pre-push files), requires the PR's required checks to have passed, and confirms the corresponding `starhaven-io/pinprick` release is published. It then creates the next patch tag (for example `v0.4.2` to `v0.4.3`) and the GitHub release.

Human-authored or unrelated changes to those files land on a clean no-op skip, and the run resumes safely if the tag or release was already created during a partial run. Permissions are least-privilege (`checks: read`, `contents: write`, `pull-requests: read`) and both file-list comparisons use `LC_ALL=C sort` so they are locale-independent on the runner.

Validated with actionlint, `zizmor --persona auditor`, and `just check`.

author: starshipsuperjam
body:
Closes #446

> *A green mechanical check below shows this change conforms to the engine's rules — not that it is correct. What covers correctness is the behavioural steps in **Review** and your own read of the change; a green check is never a substitute for that. **Your merge is the binding gate.***

## Purpose

**Close the disclosed residual where a session left idle mid-tidy never gets its later half summarized.**

- The memory tidy-up marked a session "done" after one pass and never revisited it, so a session left running-but-idle long enough to be tidied mid-run had its later turns never folded into recall — reflection skipped, though raw notes always stayed in the ledger.
- The fix teaches the tidy-sweep to pick a session back up for notes added after it was last tidied, without raising the liveness threshold that keeps the tidy prompt.

*Impact: the deferred-reflection edge from PR #443 is closed for the normal case; a later half is recovered on a subsequent boot instead of being lost to the reflection record.*

## Scope

**The consolidation marker becomes a per-session high-water-mark, and detect/read/store re-tidy only the residual beyond it.**

- The `consolidated` marker gains a `through_seq` high-water field (reusing capture's existing per-message `seq`); the effective per-session watermark is the maximum across a session's markers (monotonic, revival-safe).
- One shared watermark authority and one shared genuine-delta predicate drive detection, the `read` verb, and the store, so they cannot drift; the store recomputes the residual beyond the watermark under the single-writer ledger lock.
- Termination is structural: an examined-but-unsummarizable tail (an explicit empty store) still advances the watermark, so the sweep settles instead of re-firing; the directive instructs the tidy subagent to record an examined-empty session accordingly.
- A pre-existing (legacy) marker with no `through_seq` is projected from its timestamp boundary into sequence space, so an existing ledger is not re-consolidated wholesale on rollout.
- Markers pass compaction verbatim (never collapsed — a marker's batch keeps its pass's summaries live), so the watermark survives; the erasure boundary is bounded to markers that actually produced a summary, so an examined-but-unsummarized tail is never made erasure-eligible.

*Impact: incremental consolidation implements the re-litigated design of record (engine-planning D-307/D-308) with the durability, concurrency, and erasure guarantees intact.*

## Out of scope

**Two accepted approximations are recorded, not closed here.**

- Legacy-marker rollout under coarse (whole-second) timestamps or clock skew can, one time, re-summarize a few already-summarized turns into duplicate summaries; duplicates are recoverable and later retired, and #446 narrows this by re-summarizing such tails on the next boot before they age into any erasure window.
- Consolidation markers now accumulate one per re-tidy pass per session and are never reclaimed by compaction (a marker carries both the watermark and its pass's recall-closure, so it cannot be collapsed without orphaning summaries); the count is bounded by re-tidy cycles and is small in practice — a future slice that wants to reclaim them must first decouple the two roles.

*Impact: these are bounded, non-content-losing trade-offs disclosed for awareness, not gaps in the delivered behavior.*

## Risk

**The one irreversible boundary (physical erasure) was touched; no engine guardrail is modified.**

- The erasure-eligibility boundary was adjusted so an empty termination marker cannot pull the clock forward over un-reflected content; this was the one content-loss path found in review, is fixed, re-audited cold, and repro-verified (an un-summarized tail is not erasure-eligible while a genuinely-summarized turn still is).
- No engine guardrail is weakened or touched: the changed files are memory tools, not enforcement scripts, check-referenced scripts, or protection files, so under the property-based guarded set (D-268) `engine-guard` passes and no guardrail acknowledgment is required.
- Content is never at risk in either direction: raw notes stay resident and recoverable; the fix can only ever retain more raw, never erase more.

*Impact: the change is safe from a content-durability standpoint and needs no guardrail acknowledgment; the maintainer's merge remains the binding gate.*

## Validation

**The full self-test suite and the mechanical floor pass; the derived index files are in sync.**

- `python -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` — 3520 tests pass (2 environment-skipped); 13 new tests cover seq-0 detection, incremental re-tidy, termination, legacy projection, concurrent-sweep no-op, revival-race abort, watermark-survives-compaction, marker-not-erasure-target, the two-marker erasure boundary, and telemetry backlog re-growth.
- `python tools/validate.py --suite CI` passes except one pre-existing offline artifact (`disposition-issue-resolution` needs a GitHub token absent locally; identical on a clean tree; CI with a token is its witness).
- `knowledge_gen.py check` and `self_map.py` report both derived files in sync with the changed surfaces.

*Impact: the mechanical floor is green; the one non-green item is a known local-only token limitation orthogonal to this change.*

## Review

**A thorough two-gate cold review ran: a four-lens plan gate before building and a five-lens deliverable gate after; all blocking and serious findings were resolved.**

- Plan gate (before any code): four independent cold lenses — design soundness, buildability, operator intent, and risk/governance — caught two blocking issues (an unsummarizable tail would re-fire forever; a first-turn session could be missed) and several serious ones (legacy-marker rollout, single-source watermark, erasure-boundary scope); all were folded into the design before building.
- Deliverable gate (after building): five independent cold lenses — spec conformance, an adversarial divergence hunter, technical integrity, security/governance, and usability. Conformance and divergence found no blocking/serious issue; technical integrity found only accepted nits; security/governance found one blocking content-loss path at the erasure boundary; usability found two wording nits.
- Dispositions: the blocking erasure-boundary finding was fixed in this change and re-audited by a fresh cold security pass (no findings); the two usability nits (a self-contradictory demo line, an ambiguous directive instruction) were fixed; the technical nits and a pre-existing timestamp-tie observation are recorded in Out of scope / Risk. Several reviews ran the memory tools against throwaway temporary stores to judge behavior — never against real memory.
- The plan-gate findings were fixed before building (so reviewed and built agree); the deliverable-gate fixes were validated by the full suite, and the substantial erasure-boundary fix was additionally re-audited — the wording-only fixes were validated but not re-reviewed.

- Nothing here is something you can run yourself — there's no settled description for this project yet.

*Impact: the engine's own account of a thorough review with every blocking/serious finding resolved; the maintainer's merge is the binding gate.*

## Files of interest

**The change is concentrated in memory's consolidation and forgetting logic.**

- `.engine/tools/memory/consolidate.py` — the watermark authority (`_session_states`, `_marker_watermark`, the shared genuine-delta predicate), the residual-under-lock store, the marker `through_seq`, the `read` scoping, the termination path, and the directive/demo copy.
- `.engine/tools/memory/records.py` — the `through_seq` marker field; `.engine/tools/memory/capture.py` — the corrected lease-reaping rationale.
- `.engine/tools/memory/forget.py` — the erasure clock bounded to reflecting markers; tests in `test_consolidate.py` / `test_compact.py` / `test_forget.py` / `test_teleme

author: cbrenner04
body:
# `seq` is unique per run in the durable log

<!-- jarvis:narrative:start -->
Fix duplicate `seq` values when multiple `FileLogStream` sinks append to the same `logs.jsonl` concurrently (reconciliation + write-loop coexistence). `append()` now derives the next per-run `seq` synchronously from the durable log instead of a constructor-time in-memory counter. Adds regression tests (concurrent sinks, truncated trailing line, `follow` waiter on terminal event from a second sink) and documents the uniqueness guarantee in `v2-architecture.md` and `LogSink.append`.

Decisions:
- Allocate `seq` inside `append()` by scanning the durable log for the run's current max — not a per-instance counter or process-wide registry that can drift from the file.
- Remove the constructor-time `sequences` map/`loadSequences()` entirely; a cache would need cross-writer invalidation and is the source of the bug.
- Keep `append()` fully synchronous (read → compute next seq → `appendFileSync`); no `await` between read and write — that serializes allocation within the daemon process without a lock file.
- Cross-process writer serialization is out of scope; all sink openers live in the daemon.
- Accept per-append cost proportional to the whole `logs.jsonl` — same cost class as existing `follow()`/`tail()` full-file reads; no bounded backward scan in this correctness fix.
- Skip unparseable lines on the read path instead of throwing; truncated trailing lines are transient.
- Do not repair pre-existing duplicate `seq` in live logs; max-based allocation only prevents new duplicates.
- Leave `tail`/`follow` reader semantics unchanged (`seq` stays 1-based and monotonic per run).

author: fastestdevalive
body:
## Problem

Marking worktrees **done** on one machine hid them there, but opening vibe-station on a second machine still showed every done worktree in the sidebar.

## Root cause

The done *state* is durable and synced correctly — it's persisted server-side in the daemon manifest and served identically to every client (all sessions are tmux-backed, and the tmux poller/manifest reload preserve `done`).

What did **not** sync was the **"hide done/inactive worktrees" filter**:
- It defaulted to `false` (`useStore.ts`).
- It was persisted **only in each browser's `localStorage`** (`vibestation:workspace`), never on the daemon.

So the machine where the filter was toggled on hid done worktrees, while a different browser (its own localStorage, default off) listed them all.

## Fix

- Flip the `hideInactiveWorktrees` default to `true`.
- Bump the persisted-store version `4 → 5` with a migration so already-visited browsers pick up the new default instead of keeping their old persisted `false`.
- Update `LeftSidebar` tests to set `hideInactiveWorktrees: false` explicitly, so worktree-visibility assertions don't depend on the product default.

This is a lightweight, per-browser fix. It does **not** touch the done/lifecycle logic (which was already correct). If we later want the toggle state itself to sync live between clients, that's a follow-up (a daemon-side `ui-prefs` endpoint).

### Note
The migration force-sets `true` for every existing browser on next load, so anyone who had *deliberately* turned the filter off will see it flip back on once (easily re-toggled). That's the tradeoff for making existing browsers adopt the new default automatically.

## Testing
- `npm run typecheck` ✅
- `npm test` ✅ (123 passed)

author: hatter6822
body:
## What

Removes the seven-value **rating label** pill ("New", "Getting Attention", "Deepening", "Needs Context", "Under Review", "Resolved Context", "Bridge Active") and redesigns the story-card signal row around small, icon-first **content-integrity signals** that show how the story's record is actually evolving:

| Signal | Rendering | Backing data |
|---|---|---|
| Story dispute badge | `Challenged` / `Incorrect` / `Validated` (existing `DisputeBadge`, unchanged) | `dispute_status` (story column, WS-T) |
| Under review | eye icon + "Under review" | `safety_state` ∈ {`under-review`, `restricted`} |
| Sources | link icon + count | published comments carrying ≥1 citation — the SAME count as the comment section's "Sources" view (`sources_count`, new wire field) |
| Corrections tally | hourglass / check / X + counts | new wire object `corrections { active, validated, incorrect }`: live WS-T comment arenas, comments challenged-and-validated, comments corrected as incorrect |

The story's own posture rides the dispute badge and is **excluded** from the tally, so one debate is never double-reported. Chips render only when non-empty — a quiet story carries no chip row (the honest neutral floor). Every count carries a full sr-only expansion ("3 sourced comments", never a bare number); same-hue solid/soft pair stays ≥3:1 distinct (WS-B.2.3).

## Why

A single derived prose label compressed several orthogonal dimensions (safety, SCOI divergence, lifecycle, attention) into one vague word. The signal row conveys the concrete facts in less space, and follows the same doctrine as the earlier "Well-Sourced"/EvidenceCard removal: sourcing and correctness surface as descriptive counts and adjudicated outcomes, never as quality verdicts. Strictly no-applause: all counts are citation-/adjudication-derived, none are engagement counts.

## How

- **Shared**: `rating_label` removed from `feedItemSchema` (detail inherits); new `sources_count` + `corrections` fields with defaults, so pre-redesign offline/cached items stay wire-valid. `utils/rating-label.ts` → `utils/story-safety.ts` (keeps `deriveStorySafetyState`; deletes `deriveRatingLabel`).
- **API**: new shared batched derivation `storyCardSignals` (`apps/api/src/forum/card-signals.ts`) used by BOTH the WS-I feed (ranked + fallback paths) and `GET /v1/stories/:id`, so the surfaces agree by construction. author: skeyelab
body:
## Two critical fixes for the primary product, written weeks ago, never merged

Both were sitting on `feat/esp-019-keyboard-transport`. Cherry-picked clean (`e8c7c22`, `f7045a7`).

I spent last night saying *"the P4 got this fix, the Touch didn't."* **That was wrong.** The fixes were written and never landed. Neither firmware had them.

## 1. The clock task ran at priority 6 — below lwIP (ESP-018)

```c
-    xTaskCreate(clock_out_task, "clock_out", 4096, NULL, 6, NULL);
+    xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(clock_out_task, "clock_out", 4096, NULL, 19, NULL, 1);
```

lwIP's `tcpip_task` sits at **18**. The clock generator sat at **6**. So the network stack could legally preempt the clock — and on the analyzer, against a live Link session, **the 24-PPQN clock stopped for 611–766 ms** when the web UI was served.

19 is the deliberate sandwich: **above lwIP (18)** so serving the web UI cannot deschedule the clock, **below WiFi (23)** because starving the radio loses the Link session, and a perfectly-timed clock with no tempo is worth nothing.

X32Link and the Touch have been at 19/core-1 since ESP-018. **KitchenSync — the primary product — never got it.**

## 2. MIDI Start was emitted AFTER the downbeat clock (ESP-023)

Master's `ks_main.c` emitted the clock fan-out first and transport second. A slave begins playing on the **first clock it receives after a Start** — so the downbeat `0xF8` arrived before the `0xFA`, the slave discarded it, and began on the *next* tick. **One 24-PPQN pulse late, on every start, forever: 20.8 ms at 120 BPM.**

That is *"the drum machine falls behind when I start it from stopped."*

Verified fixed on the Touch last night on the analyzer (#96): the `0xFA` now precedes the downbeat `0xF8` by exactly **320.0 µs** — one MIDI byte time at 31250 baud. This lands the same ordering on the P4.

Order is now transport (line 247) → clock (line 263).

## Why this keeps happening

This is the same disease as ADR-0009 / ESP-026: the clock writer exists twice, so a fix lands in one firmware and the other quietly keeps the bug. Here it's worse — the fix landed in **neither**, because the branch never merged.

57/57 host suites. `check_docs` passes.

**Not hardware-verified on the P4** — the bench rig is the classic ESP32 running KitchenSyncTouch. The ordering is the same code path already analyzer-verified on the Touch, and the priority change is a one-line port of a fix proven on two other firmwares.

author: ssiyad
body:
Traffic arriving via Cloudflare has $remote_addr set to the Cloudflare edge IP, so proxy logs, rate limiting and everything downstream see Cloudflare instead of the client. Trust Cloudflare's published ranges and take the client address from CF-Connecting-IP.

Only the proxy needs this: app servers already trust the proxy via realip on X-Real-IP (templates/nginx/nginx.conf.jinja2), and all proxy location blocks already forward X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-For from $remote_addr, so the recovered address propagates to benches and Frappe unchanged.

The ranges are hardcoded from https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v4 and /ips-v6 (fetched 2026-07-13). They change rarely and agent releases are the natural refresh vehicle. Spoofing is not possible: realip only rewrites connections originating from the listed ranges, and Cloudflare always overwrites CF-Connecting-IP itself.

Verified in docker (nginx:1.27-alpine, source IP inside a Cloudflare range): header from trusted range rewrites $remote_addr; spoofed header from an untrusted source is ignored; missing or garbage header leaves the connection address untouched.

author: benzsevern
body:
Fixes the silent drop of compound `CustomRule` blocking rules carrying `IS NOT NULL` guard conjuncts -- measured at ~28pp pairwise recall on the reporter's 1M production dedupe (blocked on 3 of 6 keys).

## Root cause

The recognizer already handled multi-field conjunctions, Splink-4 paren-wrapping, quoted identifiers, and same-column SUBSTR conjuncts. The one gap: `l.first_name IS NOT NULL` guard conjuncts matched neither blocking regex, and one unrecognized conjunct drops the whole rule.

## Why recognize-and-ignore is faithful

GM's blocker already implements the guard semantics: multi-field block keys are built with `pl.concat_str` (nulls poison the whole key) and null/sentinel keys are filtered before blocks form (`blocker.py`, the #372/#375 machinery). A row with a null in any key field forms no block via that key -- exactly what Splink's `IS NOT NULL` guards express. So:

- guard on a **key column** -> ignored exactly, `report.info` (does not trip `strict=True`)
- guard on a **non-key column** -> rule still converts, `report.warn` (candidates are a superset; GM cannot express a null constraint on a non-key column) -- mirrors the file's SUBSTR-widening convention
- **guards-only** rule -> dropped with the existing unrecognized warn (nothing to block on)

## Testing

The issue's two verbatim production rules convert to `fields=["first_name","last_name"]` / `["last_name","phone_number"]` with zero warnings; Splink-4 paren+quoted variants; strict=True gated both ways; settings-level test mixing a simple rule + a guarded compound rule emits both keys. 82 passed across the four from_splink test files; ruff + pyright clean. Reviewed (spec-compliance + quality): approved, edge probes confirmed fullmatch discipline, SUBSTR-key guard membership, and ReDoS-linear pattern.

Closes #1783

body:
Surfaces a set of Clang C++ API members on the high-level managed layer that were already bridged through libclang / libClangSharp but not yet exposed. Each addition maps to a faithful Clang C++ method and is purely managed-side (no native `libClangSharp` changes), so it needs no native rebuild.

`Type`
- `AddressSpace` -- `QualType::getAddressSpace()`
- `NonReferenceType` -- `QualType::getNonReferenceType()`
- Structural / single-builtin predicates (`IsArrayType`, `IsRecordType`, `IsEnumeralType`, `IsFunctionType`, `IsReferenceType`, `IsLValueReferenceType`, `IsRValueReferenceType`, `IsMemberPointerType`, `IsBlockPointerType`, `IsVectorType`, `IsAtomicType`, `IsVoidType`, `IsBooleanType`, `IsNullPtrType`, `IsPODType`, ...) and `SizeOf` / `AlignOf` / `Nullability` conveniences

`MemberPointerType`
- `ClassType` -- `MemberPointerType::getClass()`

`CXXMethodDecl`
- `IsPureVirtual` -- `CXXMethodDecl::isPureVirtual()`

`FieldDecl`
- `OffsetOfField` -- field offset (bits)

`TemplateName`
- `Kind` / `IsNull`

----------

Only trivially-correct predicates are done managed-side; multi-kind / subtle predicates (e.g. `isScalarType`, `isArithmeticType`) and entirely-unbridged concepts (`NestedNameSpecifier`, `DeclarationName`, `Designator`, `LambdaCapture`, `CXXCtorInitializer`, `LambdaExpr` surfacing) are deferred to a follow-up that adds the native bridges first.

Regression tests added in `TypeTest` and `DeclTest`. Builds clean (0 warnings); all `ClangSharp.UnitTests` pass.

author: mosnin
body:
## Summary

Fixes the live white-screen crash at the last onboarding step on operate.to.

**Root cause:** the production Vercel build has no `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL`. By design, `providers.tsx` skips the `ConvexProvider` when that var is unset (so the marketing site renders before backend creds are wired) — but any app route that calls `useMutation`/`useQuery` then throws `Could not find Convex client!`. The final onboarding step is the first such component, hence "got to the last step and it crashed."

**Fix:** a `RequireBackend` guard wraps `/onboarding` and the `/dashboard` layout. When the build lacks `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL`, app routes render an actionable "Backend not configured" card (set the var and redeploy — it's inlined at build time) instead of crashing.

author: ali0600
body:
Third of the testing-deep-dive PRs: **prevention** — make silent absence impossible.

## Why
The deploy job ended at *"Triggered Render deploy"* — success meant **the curl fired**. That exact gap is how ALDI shipped green and never appeared in prod (#68): its degraded path fired on every run, and absence looks identical to "still deploying". Mechanizing this session's lesson: *verify the feature in prod, not the deploy.*

## Deploy verify (`ci.yml`)
- `/health` now exposes the **running commit** (`RENDER_GIT_COMMIT` — verified in Render's docs as available at runtime for Docker services; +unit test).
- After the hook fires, the job **polls `/health` until the merged SHA is actually live** (bounded ~15 min; if a newer merge deploys over us mid-poll, it stands down with a warning — that run's own verify covers prod), then asserts `/api/offers` serves **>0 offers**, with retries for the boot-scrape.
- The verify steps key off the hook *actually having fired*, so a secretless fork stays green.

"Is my code live yet?" becomes a queryable fact instead of an inference from data shapes.

## Weekly data-quality gate (`scrape.yml` → `.github/scripts/verify_deals.py`)
After the Sunday reset succeeds, assert the **served outcome** against measured floors:

| check | floor | catches |
|---|---|---|
| distinct chains | **≥ 5** | a silently skipped chain — pages **even when the skip was a designed degradation** (per your decision: fail-closed must announce itself; the issue auto-closes on recovery) |
| total offers | ≥ 800 | scrapers falling back to sample data |
| €/kg-sortable | ≥ 50% | Grundpreis shape drift past the parser (the bug family) |
| "other" rate | ≤ 15% | the feed's taxonomy moving under the classifier |

A violation fails the job and flows into the **existing** alert-issue + close-on-recovery machinery — no new plumbing. The script is offline-testable (`--file`) and prints counts only (the PLZ secret never echoes).

## Proven both ways — and the calibration found something
- **Passes against live prod** (5 chains, 1663 offers, 71.4% €/kg, 7.5% other).
- **Fails against a doctored 4-chain fixture** (exit 1 on the chains floor).
- Calibration corrected a stale belief: the real "other" norm is **~7.4%** (prod **and** local agree at 7.5/7.3 — measured, not inferred), not the ~1% remembered from an older week's survey. The ceiling sits at ~2× the measured norm: a smoke alarm for collapse, not a quality aspiration.

464 backend tests, ruff clean, both workflows YAML-validated. Merging this deploys (runtime `main.py` change) — **so this PR's own post-merge run is the end-to-end test of the new gate.**

body:
The published dispatcher image crash-loops on startup with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'aci_protocol'`, disabling the entire Slack path (mention ingestion + the approval-button relay) in every released image since 0.3.0.

`apps/dispatcher/src/agentos_dispatcher/{handlers.py,queue.py}` import `aci_protocol`, but `apps/dispatcher/pyproject.toml` never declared the `aci-protocol` workspace dependency. The image builds with `uv sync --no-editable`, which installs only declared deps, so the workspace member was importable from a source checkout but absent from the isolated image venv. Nothing in CI ran the dispatcher image, so it shipped broken.

- Declare `aci-protocol` in `apps/dispatcher/pyproject.toml` (mirroring `apps/worker`) and re-lock. The lock delta is 2 lines; `aci-protocol` only needs `pydantic` (already declared), so no transitive drift.
- Add a `dispatcher-image-smoke` CI job that builds the real image and asserts `import agentos_dispatcher; import aci_protocol` resolves inside the isolated venv, so a workspace-dep-not-declared regression fails red instead of reshipping.

Verified locally: the pre-fix image import check exits 1 with the exact `ModuleNotFoundError`; the post-fix image exits 0 and `python -m agentos_dispatcher` runs through the import chain to the expected missing-`SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` stage. ruff, mypy (128 files), and `pytest apps/dispatcher` (50 passed) green.

Closes #428

author: tiredithumans
body:
## Summary

Dependency audit across both trees ahead of the release.

**No major/minor bumps were available.** The root workspace and the web-rs manifests are already at their latest compatible versions. The only two outdated direct deps are the deliberate crypto pins, and their documented lifting condition ("leave them until oauth2/Tauri move first") is **still unmet**:

| Crate | Current | Latest | Blocker |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rand` | 0.8.7 | 0.10.2 | `oauth2 5.0.0` — the latest release, no v6 exists — still requires `rand 0.8` |
| `sha2` | 0.10.9 | 0.11.0 | `oauth2 5.0.0`, `secret-service 5.1.0`, and `tauri-codegen` (→ `tauri 2.11.5`, also latest) all require `sha2 0.10` |

Bumping either would **not move a dependency** — it would compile a *second* crypto major alongside the one those upstream crates still pin, which is exactly what the pin exists to prevent. Worth noting: `rand 0.10.2` already appears in `Cargo.lock`, but only via `quinn-proto`, a feature-gated QUIC path that is never built (`cargo tree -i rand@0.10.2 -e all --target all` returns nothing) — it's a lockfile ghost, not evidence the bump is free.

This PR therefore contains only what was genuinely available: a patch-level refresh of the excluded web-rs lockfile.

- `mio` 1.2.1 → 1.2.2
- `socket2` 0.6.4 → 0.6.5
- `syn` 2.0.118 → 2.0.119
- `toml` 1.1.2 → 1.1.3
- `xxhash-rust` 0.8.16 → 0.8.17

All transitive build-time deps; no manifest requirement changed, and the tree stays within the Rust 1.96 MSRV floor. Lockfile-only and not user-facing, so no CHANGELOG entry — the existing `[Unreleased]` "full dependency refresh" bullet already describes this state.

## Test plan

- [x] `just verify` — clean (exit 0)
- [x] `just audit` + `just web-audit` — clean, both trees
- [x] `just deny` + `just web-deny` — clean, both trees
- [x] Crypto invariants re-checked after the refresh: no `rsa` in either lockfile, `sha2` still a single major in the graph, `rand`/`sha2` manifest pins untouched
- [ ] `just web-itest` — not run locally (no Chrome on this box); runs in CI

author: creatorghost
body:
## Issue

`npm i -g dcode-ai` 404s: the `dcode-ai` wrapper was never published. Every `publish-npm` run fails on the 184MB `dcode-ai-windows-x64` binary with npm `E429` (publish rate limit — `as user undefined` is npm's rate-limit wording, not an auth failure; 5 of 7 platform packages publish fine with the token).

Root cause: `publish.ts` is sequential + fail-fast, and the user-facing wrapper publishes **last**. One throttled platform throws and aborts the run before the wrapper is ever published, so nothing is installable.

Registry state confirms it: `dcode-ai-{darwin-arm64,darwin-x64,linux-x64,windows-arm64}@1.0.1` are live; only `dcode-ai-windows-x64` and the `dcode-ai` wrapper are missing.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (release tooling)

## What changed

- `publish()` no longer throws; it returns success/failure and collects failures.
- Every platform that can publish does; the tiny **wrapper always publishes** regardless of a throttled platform.
- All platforms are listed as `optionalDependencies` at the target version. npm resolves only the current platform's optional dep at install time, so listing a still-rate-limited platform is harmless and self-heals when a re-run publishes it.
- Sturdier E429 handling: honors `Retry-After` when present, 8 attempts, capped exponential backoff.
- Real (non-E429) errors are logged in full; the run exits non-zero when any package is left behind so leftovers are visible. Re-running fills only the missing ones via the existing already-published skip.

## Verification

- `bun typecheck` — 30/30 pass.
- Prettier clean.
- Idempotency and the optional-dep fallback match the existing esbuild-style wrapper design documented at the top of `publish.ts`.

## Notes

- No unit-test seam exists for a live-`npm publish` script; validation is the publish workflow itself. A dispatch (dry-run then real) is the next step after merge.
- Intentional tradeoff: if a platform stays rate limited, the run still exits non-zero to flag it — but `dcode-ai` is installable in the meantime, and a re-run backfills the platform.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Improved package publishing resilience with automatic retries and rate-limit handling.
  * Added support for safely re-running publishing to process only packages that previously failed.
  * Added clearer reporting for incomplete and successful publishing runs.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Publishing failures are now handled without unexpected exceptions.
  * Dry runs complete with appropriate status reporting, while failed releases return a failure status.

author: bgarcevic
body:
## What

Implements `tx query` — previously a non-functional stub — as a real command that executes DAX (`EVALUATE`/`DEFINE`) and DMV (`SELECT ... FROM $SYSTEM....`) queries against a live model (`powerbi://`, `asazure://`, `localhost:<port>`) and renders the rowset as a table, JSON, or CSV.

```
tx query [-q <dax> | --file <path|->] [--param name=value ...] [--limit <n>]
         [-o <file>] [--no-validate]
```

Design is inspired by DaxStudio's `dscmd` CLI (query input flags, repeatable `--param`, format handling).

## How

Mirrors the `refresh` command's layering end-to-end:

- **Core**: new `IModelQuerySession` capability + `ModelQueryRequest`/`QueryColumn`/`ModelQueryResult` rowset types. Cell values are restricted to Core-safe primitives (`string`/`long`/`double`/`decimal`/`bool`/`DateTime`/null for BLANK).
- **Provider.Tom**: adds `Microsoft.AnalysisServices.AdomdClient` 19.114.0 (same pin as AMO). `TomModelQueryExecutor` opens a dedicated `AdomdConnection` reusing the existing access-token plumbing, binds `--param` via `AdomdParameter`, cancels via `command.Cancel()` on Ctrl+C, and applies `--limit` client-side (reads limit+1 rows to detect truncation — server-side TOPN wrapping would break `DEFINE` blocks and DMV syntax). No ADOMD types cross the provider boundary.
- **App**: `QueryModelHandler` resolves the target like refresh (primary if remote, else remote workspace-mode secondary), pre-validates that the query starts with `EVALUATE`/`DEFINE`/`SELECT` (comment-aware; `--no-validate` bypasses), and maps failures to new `TOMIX_QUERY_*` codes documented in `docs/error-codes.md`.
- **Cli**: `QueryCommand` (input precedence: `-q`/`--file` conflict → exit 2, `-` sentinel or implicit pipe → stdin) and `QueryResultRenderer` (dynamic-column table with right-aligned numerics, row-count/duration footer on **stderr** so stdout stays pipeable, CSV with ISO-8601 dates, `-o` writes BOM-less json/csv inferred from the extension).

## Notes for review

- The JSON output shape (`server`/`database`/`columns`/`rows`/`rowCount`/`truncated`/`durationMs`) is pinned by `QueryResultJsonContractTests` and designed to be additive-safe for the deferred perf fields.
- The old stub's perf flags (`--trace`, `--cold`, `--plan`, `--runs`) are **omitted entirely**, not stubbed — they need XMLA trace plumbing (`refresh --trace` is the pattern) and land in a follow-up PR; re-adding flags is additive.
- `TomServerModelSession` now carries its `ModelReference` (needed to rebuild the ADOMD connection string with the resolved catalog), which touched two existing provider test files.
- Verified live from macOS against a Power BI XMLA endpoint: table/JSON/CSV output, DMV + `--limit` truncation, `--param` round-trip, server-error → `TOMIX_QUERY_FAILED` exit 1, and all usage-error paths (exit 2 with hints). AdomdClient 19.114.0 ships a managed net8.0 lib and works cross-platform with token auth.

## Testing

- `dotnet build && dotnet test`: 825 tests, all green.
- New: `QueryModelHandlerTests` (validation, target resolution, capability guard, error mapping, rowset/limit/param forwarding), `QueryCommandParseTests` (`--limit` validator, input conflicts, `--param` parsing, `-o` format resolution), `QueryResultJsonContractTests` (JSON field names + cell serialization, deterministic CSV cells).

author: webjema
body:
## Problem

An empty tmux `-t` selector resolves to the session's **active** window, so `tmux kill-window -t ""` kills whatever tab is focused - the firstmate coordinator's own - instead of no-op'ing. Reclaiming a **detached** crew whose window was already closed ran teardown with an empty `window=` (`fm-detach.sh` drops `window=` and records `detached_window=` instead), and the tmux backend's `fm_backend_tmux_kill ""` then self-destructed. Reproduced live twice.

## Fix (defense in depth, root cause first)

- `fm_backend_tmux_kill` (`bin/backends/tmux.sh`) refuses an empty target (`[ -n "$1" ] || return 0`) and owns the "empty target is dangerous" contract in its header.
- `fm_backend_kill` (`bin/fm-backend.sh`) guards the same before dispatching to any backend (also hardens `fm-bootstrap.sh`'s liveness-sweep kill).
- `fm-teardown.sh` falls back to `detached_window=` when `window=` is absent, so a detached-reclaimed task's kill target is never empty - and a still-present detached window is still cleaned up.

## Tests (MOCKED tmux only - never a live empty-target kill)

- `fm-backend.test.sh`: the empty target never reaches `kill-window` (primitive + dispatcher), while a non-empty target still does.
- `fm-detach.test.sh` case (i): reclaiming a windowless detached meta issues no empty-target kill.
- Both fail before the guard and pass after (verified by reverting the source).

## Docs

`docs/tmux-backend.md` records the empty-target hazard from the incident (tmux 3.4), without reproducing a live empty-target kill.

## Verification

`bin/fm-lint.sh` clean; full suite 64/64 passed; real-tmux smoke test confirms non-empty kills still work.

author: galletas1712
body:
## Summary

- add `history.fork` and a `/fork` workflow for managed project sessions
- reuse the same strict target, boundary, revision, branch, idle, and running-delegation semantics as `history.switch`
- copy the complete transcript forest into an independent top-level session while selecting the requested switch-valid boundary
- clone the source session's current idle cwd, including dirty and untracked files, into the child workspace

## Design

Switching and forking share the parts that must not drift:

- one typed daemon history-target parser and preflight
- one row-locked store validator for active work, running delegations, active-leaf/revision fences, boundary membership, and compaction-aware branch IDs
- self-documenting store request structs rather than positional optional arguments
- one web target-preparation path and stale-history refresh path

They remain separate where behavior genuinely differs:

- switch updates the source session's active leaf and selected-session cache
- fork snapshots the current workspace, creates a new session, stores fork provenance, and cold-navigates to the child

Workspace cloning is serialized with daemon-managed cwd writers and read-only subagent snapshots. `.pi-handoff` is excluded across Btrfs, reflink, and copy backends, and clone cleanup is symlink-safe and collision-safe.

## Semantics

- fork is managed-project-only
- both switch and fork require an idle source with no running delegation
- filesystem contents come from fork time, not the selected historical transcript point
- the full transcript forest, compaction roots, sibling branches, and provider replay data are preserved
- queues, actions, event history, delegations, subagent relationships, archival state, and compaction runtime state are not inherited
- title, auto-title preference, compaction policy, provider configuration, and MCP manifest are retained; the system prompt is rerendered for the child cwd

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo check -p agent-store -p agent-daemon --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy -p agent-store -p agent-daemon --all-targets`
- PostgreSQL-backed `cargo test -p agent-store`: **72 passed**

body:
Zwei Fachentscheidungen aus dem Bug-Review umgesetzt (vom Nutzer freigegeben):

## 1. Fristberechnung nach § 108 AO i.V.m. § 187 Abs. 1, § 188 Abs. 2 BGB
Der Anschaffungstag zählt nicht mit; die Frist endet erst mit Ablauf des Jahrestags.
- **Spekulation (§ 23 EStG)** – Verkauf **am** 10-Jahres-Jahrestag ist noch steuerpflichtig, steuerfrei erst am Folgetag. Vorher meldete die App den Jahrestag selbst schon als „steuerfrei" — die für den Nutzer **riskante** Richtung (er hätte sich auf steuerfrei verlassen und Steuer nachzahlen müssen).
- **15%-Fenster (§ 6 Abs. 1 Nr. 1a EStG)** – der Jahrestag gehört noch ins schädliche Fenster (vorher einen Tag zu kurz, dadurch leicht unter-warnend).

## 2. Verbilligte Vermietung (§ 21 Abs. 2 EStG)
Eine **separate** Stellplatzmiete wurde bisher nur in die Ist-Warmmiete (Zähler), aber nicht in den Vergleichswert gerechnet. Das hob den Prozentsatz künstlich Richtung 100 % und konnte eine echte Verbilligung fälschlich „grün" zeigen. Stellplatz bleibt jetzt außen vor (kein Wohnungs-Vergleichswert vorhanden); ein mit der Wohnung vermieteter Stellplatz ist über die Kaltmiete ohnehin erfasst.

Tests an die korrigierte Semantik angepasst — **123 grün**, Build sauber. Die betroffenen Alt-Tests hatten die falsche Logik festgeschrieben.

> Weiterhin keine Steuerberatung — reine Rechenhilfen. Beide Änderungen bewegen die Anzeige in die konservative (nutzerschützende) Richtung.
