author: ashfaknawshad
body:
First of two dark-mode passes. This one introduces a reusable semantic colour palette and converts the small, zero-token pages — validating the token set before the heavy pages get the same treatment.

## The problem

Dark mode is driven by CSS custom properties under `[data-theme="dark"]` in `globals.css`. A page follows the theme **only if it reads `var(--…)` tokens**. Many pages hardcoded hex (`bg-[#f6f7fb]`) and Tailwind palette classes (`bg-green-50`, `text-red-700`) instead — so they stayed light in dark mode. The **notifications page** was the most visible: it used zero tokens.

## New tokens

`globals.css` gains a semantic status palette, light + dark:

| Token | Role |
|---|---|
| `--success` / `--success-tint` / `--success-border` | success cards, badges |
| `--warn` / `--warn-tint` / `--warn-border` | warnings |
| `--danger` / `--danger-tint` / `--danger-border` | errors, destructive |
| `--info` / `--info-tint` / `--info-border` | info/default |

- **Light values are the exact Tailwind shades the UI already used** (green-700 on green-50, etc.), so light mode is pixel-unchanged.
- **Dark values are hand-picked** — the light shades can't be reused (green-700 on charcoal is illegible), so the tint becomes a deep desaturated wash and the base lightens to sit on it.
- **All 16 base-on-tint pairs clear WCAG AA (≥ 4.5:1)** in both themes — verified with a contrast script (lowest: success/warn ~4.8 in light; all dark pairs ≥ 6).

## Pages converted

- **notifications** — every colour (per-type cards, the on-device warning, NEW badge, header/back/clear). Also swapped two inline `lang === "si" ? … : …` ternaries for the existing `t.back` / `t.clearAll` strings.
- **reset**, **profile/query** — backgrounds, surfaces, text, inputs, error box, buttons.
- **login** — the error message only. The branded dark hero panel keeps its `bg-white/10` (intentionally dark, not a bug).

## Not in this PR

`answer` (86 hardcoded sites), `analysis/[documentID]` (91), and `bulk-review` (33) — the heavy screens — are a separate follow-up so this palette can be reviewed on small surfaces first.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors / 34 warnings (identical to `main` baseline); `npm run build` passes. The three small pages have **0 residual hardcoded colours**. Not manually viewed in a browser (dev server wasn't up) — but this is a mechanical token swap with light values chosen to match the prior hardcoded ones, so light mode is unchanged by construction; worth a dark-mode glance on notifications when convenient.

author: mmagician
body:
Closes #3344

Adds the developer-facing pricing API so a network account developer can configure their fee policy from benchmarked numbers instead of hand-picking them.

## What this adds

- `NoteConsumptionCost` trait, implemented by every priced note type in `miden-standards` and `miden-agglayer`
- Root-keyed cost lookups matching how `BasicConstantFeePolicy` and `estimate_note_fee` are keyed: `StandardNote::note_cost` and `AgglayerNote::note_cost` (on the new `AgglayerNote` enum mirroring `StandardNote`), the latter falling back to the standard notes so a single lookup covers both
- [BREAKING] `TransactionFee` moved from `miden-protocol`'s testing module to `miden_protocol::transaction` as the single Rust mirror of the kernel fee formula `verification_base_fee * (ilog2(cycles) + 1)` (unconditional `+ 1`, matching `compute_fee` in `tx.masm`); the now-unused `TransactionMeasurements::trace_length` was removed
- `NetworkNotePricer`: builds on `TransactionFee` and adds a safety margin in verification cycles. The default margin of 1 prices a note as if it consumed twice its measured cycles, absorbing moderate cost growth (e.g. the pending sponsorship-collection integration in `AuthNetworkAccount`) between benchmark regenerations
- Recursive pricing per the issue: `price(N) = fee(cycles(N)) + sum(price(M))` over the notes created by consuming N, conservatively assuming all created notes target network accounts. The PSWAP self-recursion is cut off at one level of nesting
- `BasicConstantFeePolicy::with_fees` installs the priced entries, so the end-to-end configuration is:

```rust
let pricer = NetworkNotePricer::builder()
    .fee_parameters(fee_parameters)
    .lookup(AgglayerNote::note_cost)
    .build();
let policy = BasicConstantFeePolicy::new().with_fees([
    (P2idNote::script_root(), pricer.price(P2idNote::script_root())?),
    (ClaimNote::script_root(), pricer.price(ClaimNote::script_root())?),
]);
```

author: lararosekelley
body: fix(forge): detect review requests routed to your teams A review requested from a team you belong to never matched you: `viewer_requested_now` only checked individual `requested_reviewers`. That's the higharc/product#22693 miss. Add `requested_teams` to the forge PR model and match it against your team memberships. The GitHub source fetches your teams via `GET /user/teams` (needs `read:org`; best-effort - it warns and skips if the token can't list them) and passes them as `org/slug` keys into the diff, so a team request matches when one of your teams *in the PR's org* is requested. The persisted snapshot records the team-based request too, so it edge-detects and won't re-fire. GitHub only for now; Gitea has no team-request model yet, so it passes an empty set. author: joshkappler
body:
## Summary - add `gt generate --pseudo`: emits a pseudo-localized translation file (default `en-XA`, the CLDR pseudo locale `Intl` names "Pseudo-Accents", so it lists normally in ``; any valid locale works) so layout bugs surface before buying a translation. Accents expose hardcoded strings, roughly 40% expansion exposes truncation, bracket markers expose clipping and concatenation - the transform preserves structure: ICU parses through core's own `traverseIcu`/`printIcuAst` (only literal text accented; arguments, plural/select structure, tags, and `#` untouched), JSX trees walk recursively, and strings that fail ICU parsing fall back to plain accenting instead of throwing - guardrails: the pseudo target may not be the default locale or a configured real locale (either would overwrite real content), pseudo files fully regenerate on every run, and plain `gt generate` skips pseudo-region locales in its merge loop - fixes a real runtime bug found while building: `isSameDialect('en', 'en-XA')` returned true, so `requiresTranslation` said no and gt-react never fetched the pseudo file. The unspecified-region leniency that makes `en` match `en-US` is now scoped so a CLDR pseudo region only matches itself, with `en`/`en-US` unchanged and pinned by tests ## Testing - 29 transform/flag tests, 4 handler wiring tests, 9 dialect-semantics tests, the behavior-defining ones written first - full library suites green locally (format 258, cli 2101, core 592, 29 turbo tasks); the gt-next swc wasm build needs cargo, so CI covers it; `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` clean - end to end in `examples/vite-create-app`: ran the built CLI, inspected the emitted `en-XA.json`, built and served the production build, drove a real browser. The selector lists the pseudo locale, bracketed text renders with the live counter still incrementing inside it, and switching back renders plain source - adversarially reviewed pre-submission (five finder lenses, twelve claims, two skeptics each); every confirmed finding fixed, including two vendored-FormatJS printer quirks (escaped `#` reprints losslessly behind an opt-in `escapeAllPounds`; default output stays byte-identical since hashing depends on it) ## Notes - exports `traverseIcu`/`printIcuAst` from `generaltranslation/internal`, the path core already uses - FormatJS, Lingui, Lokalise, Android, and Microsoft all ship pseudo-localization; none of the compiler-based i18n stacks do - docs live outside this repo since #727; a docs page for the flag follows once this lands - changesets: gt minor, generaltranslation minor, @generaltranslation/format patch

Greptile Summary

This PR adds `--pseudo [locale]` to `gt generate`, emitting a pseudo-localized translation file (default `en-XA`) for layout testing. It also fixes a runtime bug where `isSameDialect('en', 'en-XA')` returned `true`, causing gt-react to skip fetching pseudo-locale files. - **`packages/cli/src/translation/pseudo.ts`** — new pseudo-localization engine with accent mapping, ~40% expansion padding, and bracket wrapping for ICU/JSX/i18next/STRING formats; guarded by `resolvePseudoLocale` and `isPseudoLocale`. - **`packages/format/src/locales/isSameDialect.ts`** — scopes region-unspecified leniency so CLDR pseudo regions (XA, XB) only match themselves; `en`/`en-US` matching is unchanged. - **`packages/core/src/derive/utils/printIcuAst.ts`** — adds opt-in `escapeAllPounds` for lossless reprinting of literal `#` in plural options; default output stays byte-identical for hashing.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge; all changed paths are additive or narrowly-scoped fixes, the isSameDialect change is backed by 9 dialect-semantics tests, and the printIcuAst default output is byte-identical to preserve existing hashing. The pseudo-localization path is entirely additive. The isSameDialect fix is carefully scoped so ordinary en/en-US matching is unchanged. The printIcuAst escapeAllPounds option defaults off, keeping the existing byte-identical hash path intact. The CLI change wraps pseudo generation after the real-locale merge loop and includes proper early-exit guards throughout. **Files Needing Attention:** No files require special attention; the one open question is whether the changeset bump type (patch vs minor) matches the project's release conventions.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | packages/cli/src/translation/pseudo.ts | New pseudo-localization engine; ICU path mutates a freshly-parsed AST (safe), JSX walk is non-mutating, i18next split regex is correct, and all four data-format paths are tested. | | packages/format/src/locales/isSameDialect.ts | pseudoRegionMismatch correctly fires when any locale carries XA/XB but not all locales have a region, leaving en/en-US behaviour unchanged while blocking en/en-XA cross-matches. | | packages/core/src/derive/utils/printIcuAst.ts | escapeAllPounds option threads correctly through plural, select, tag, and literal nodes; default path is byte-identical to upstream printAST as verified by the added test. | | packages/cli/src/cli/inline.ts | Pseudo locale resolved early (fail-fast), merge loop skips XA/XB locales, pseudo file fully regenerated after real-locale writes, error path for missing gt output path is handled. | | .changeset/cli-pseudo-localization.md | Uses 'patch' for both 'gt' and 'generaltranslation', while the PR description states 'minor' — new exported symbols and a new CLI flag are additive features that conventionally warrant a minor bump. | | packages/core/src/internal.ts | Exports traverseIcu and printIcuAst from the internal path; both were already used internally so this is a non-breaking additive change. | | packages/cli/src/cli/__tests__/generatePseudo.test.ts | Covers four key handler scenarios: default pseudo locale write, skip-then-regenerate for configured XA locale, no pollution on plain generate, and rejection of a configured real locale. | | packages/cli/src/translation/__tests__/pseudo.test.ts | 29 tests cover ICU plurals/tags/skeletons/escaped-#/invalid-fallback, i18next interpolations and $t nesting, JSX strings/variables/elements/branches/content-props/aria-ids, buildPseudoTranslations, isPseudoLocale, and resolvePseudoLocale. |

Flowchart

When a ship-flow PR merges — even via a direct `gh pr merge` that bypasses the
FO flow — the entity now converges to done+archive through one authority instead
of three competing paths that silently disagreed.

## What changed
- Consolidate the three divergent closeout paths onto `spacedock merge guard`
  behind one `bin/closeout-adapter.sh` (renamed from merged-pr-closeout-reconciler.sh).
- Delegate every trigger to it: the SessionStart drift hook, the `_mods/pr-merge.md`
  startup/idle hooks, and the manual CLI.
- Normalize `gh` MERGED → a durable `pr=pr-merge:{N}` sentinel; fail closed with
  `state-driver unavailable`; defer (never mutate) on dirty tree / wrong branch / stale trunk.
- Emit a non-blocking `debrief_due` signal on finalize; document convergence in
  `references/pr-merge-paths.md` + README.

- test-closeout-adapter.sh 148/148, test-warn-state-drift.sh 69/69 passed.
- Full ship-flow shell suite + node + version-triple + no-dangling: green (incl. under a

- Live-probe: adapter → real spacedock 0.25.0 `merge guard` end-to-end convergence
  verified (finalize + debrief_due + idempotent replay), not just against a stub.

The safety gates in `bin/closeout-adapter.sh` (trunk / dirty / sentinel / recovery)
carry the most subtlety; deeper crash/replay-path edge-hardening is tracked as a

## Summary

`summarize`'s `relative` and `roas`/`cost-per` rows divide by the counterfactual/treated post-period sums, so a panel whose post-period sums to zero raised `ZeroDivisionError` — even though the neighbouring `_get_roas` already guards its denominators with `inf`.

Adds a regression test running `relative` / `roas` / `cost-per` on a zero-sum panel — it raises `ZeroDivisionError` without the fix and reports `inf` with it.

- `pytest` — **257 passed** (254 + 3 new)

Behavior change is limited to the previously-crashing degenerate case.

author: jenner-analytics
body:
[Jenneranalytics.com](https://jenneranalytics.com) provides an API that runs SAS code, with support for more than 200 SAS procedures. You can also use it with AI assistants in a collaborative workspace. It's available for Mac on the Apple App Store, and by license for Windows and Linux.

We support the larger community by
(1) increasing access to SAS-compatible systems,
(2) by providing test coverage and a test coverage framework to public SAS repos in order to encourage the use of best practices in software engineering.

Your demographic_summary code.sas runs on Jenner unmodified — this PR adds a small compatibility bundle so you can see for yourself. It's the test we wrote for your project, shared in case it's useful, and was assembled with AI assistance as is most code in modern businesses today.

The `TRT=2; OUTPUT;` trick in the DATA DM1 step — re-emitting every row under a synthetic treatment code to get a free "Overall" column out of the same PROC TRANSPOSE/PROC FREQ machinery you already wrote for the two real arms — is a neat piece of SAS economy, and it's reused consistently across all four blocks (Age, Gender, Ethnicity, Race) with the same ORDER/Desc stacking pattern feeding the final PROC REPORT. That's a well-structured TLF for a first pass at Table 14.1.2.1.

`jenner-check/` contains one bundle built from that script:

```
jenner-check/
├── README.md
├── run_jenner.sh
└── t001_demographic_summary/
    ├── script.sas       # your demographic_summary code.sas, adapted only to read inline sample data
    ├── autoexec.sas
    ├── expected.json
    ├── meta.json
    └── expected/
        ├── log.txt
        └── output.txt
```

The only change from your original: the PROC IMPORT that pointed at a local Windows xlsx path is replaced with a small inline DATALINES block (20 mock subjects, same TRT/AGE/GENDER/ETHNIC/RACE columns) so the script runs standalone — every DATA step and PROC call after that is untouched. The captured run reproduces your Table 14.1.2.1 layout end to end, including the PROC REPORT COMPUTE header/footer lines.

To try it yourself: check out this PR's branch and run from the repo root —

```bash
gh pr checkout 1
curl -sS --data-binary @jenner-check/t001_demographic_summary/script.sas https://api.jenneranalytics.com/v1/quick
```

or `cd jenner-check && ./run_jenner.sh --all` to re-run the bundle and verify it against the pinned results. The hosted API is free to try, no signup — full API reference: [the docs](https://docs.jenneranalytics.com/api/).

One note on data: the runner only uploads the SAS source text of the script it runs (plus a two-line autoexec) to api.jenneranalytics.com, where it runs and returns the log and listing. It does not read or upload any data files, so anything sitting next to a script — like your Excel file — stays on your machine; nothing is sent unless you run a command yourself. It's the same as pasting a snippet into any hosted tool.

Merge it, close it, or ignore it — no response expected either way, and we won't open further PRs in this repo. If you'd rather not see PRs like this at all, a comment containing `no-more-prs`, or an issue titled `jenner-check: opt out`, will do it for good.

author: samggreenberg
body:
## Summary

VTSBrowse signpost region names in **Tags** mode are drawn from a fixed built-in vocabulary — AudioSet-527 for audio, OpenImages-600 for images. This PR adds a per-media-type override so a user can supply their **own** tag list (a domain-specific vocabulary, or one generated from another corpus) without editing packaged assets, straight from the Settings UI.

Previously this was only reachable by dropping a new `.txt` into `vtscore/projection/assets/` and registering a provider in code — not something an end user could do.

## What changed

**Backend**
- New per-user setting `browse_signpost_vocab: {media_type: [term, ...]}`. Normalized on write (trimmed, blanks + duplicates dropped order-preservingly, capped at 2000 terms — each term costs one text-embed at build time); an empty/absent list falls back to the shipped vocabulary.
- `ZeroShotTagProvider` gains an optional `vocab_terms` override and a `with_terms()` builder. The builder folds a digest of the term set into the provider `name`, so the provider `signature` — and therefore the per-media `signpost_text` cache key **and** the labeler signature — changes when the list changes. Swapping the vocabulary re-letters the map on the next build (or via the background relabel self-heal) instead of serving stale texts, exactly like the existing captioner toggle.
- The override applies whether the tag provider serves directly (Tags mode) or as the generative captioner's fallback.
- Plumbed through `CoreConfig.signpost_vocab` + the settings shim, mirroring `browse_signpost_captioner`.

**Frontend**
- Settings → Browser tab gains a **Custom tags** textarea (one term per line), shown for image/audio when in Tags mode. Empty restores the built-in list. Takes effect on the next map rebuild.

**Incidental pre-existing fixes** (surfaced while running the suite; both failed on `dev` independently of this feature)
- `tests/conftest.py` `_fake_embed_audio` hard-accessed `arg["media_path"]` and `KeyError`'d on in-memory (`media_bytes`-only) medias such as clipper output; it now seeds off `media_bytes` (preserving the "distinct clips → distinct vectors" contract).
- `test_batch_medias_includes_clip_fields` asserted the pre-suppression clip-window contract; byte-sliced audio deliberately suppresses top-level `clip_start`/`clip_end` (they reach the UI via `custom_metadata`). Updated to match the documented behavior in `vtsearch/routes/media/list.py`.

## Testing

- `./run-tests.sh` — all 6418 Python tests pass; ruff / format / codespell / deptry / pip-audit / pyright / OpenAPI-snapshot clean.
- `./run-tests.sh frontend` — Angular `build:prod`, `npm audit`, and Vitest (1701) all pass.
- New coverage: `browse_signpost_vocab` round-trip + normalization (settings API), and `with_terms` / custom-vocab selection incl. captioner-fallback interaction (`test_signpost_texts.py`).

## Notes

- No screenshot reshoot needed: the only Settings doc shot (`settings-appearance`) frames the Appearance pane, not the Browser tab.
- Backwards compatibility: no breaks — the new setting defaults to empty (built-in vocabulary), and the OpenAPI snapshot is regenerated.

**Ruling law** (docs/plans/UI-A3.md, Ratification OQ-7c): a small tests-harness chore PR (@testing-library/react + jsdom, literal pins) immediately post-A3-merge, BEFORE A4, backfilling render assertions on the moderation surfaces. Zero A3 diff; zero `src/` lines. **This PR body is the record — no dedicated log file for this chore.**

| Assertion | File | What it pins |

| R-1 | `tests/unit/composer/render/error-strip.test.tsx` | Every strip-class state renders its `copy.ts` string EXACTLY (incl. both `p3_market_race` copy variants); every elsewhere-rendered class (modal · banner · auth-gate · onboarding-route · image-affordance) renders NO strip; idle/in-flight render null |

author: strausmann
body:
## Problem
After enabling branch protection (required status checks) on `main`, the nightly/dispatch release fails: `@semantic-release/git` commits CHANGELOG.md/package.json back to `main` and **pushes directly** — which protection now rejects. Result: tags/images stop being produced (v1.9.0 release job failed).

## Fix
Remove `@semantic-release/git` (and the now-orphaned `@semantic-release/changelog`). semantic-release still: analyses commits, generates release notes, creates the git **tag** + **GitHub Release**, and the workflow builds/pushes the Docker image. No direct push to the protected branch → protection stays fully intact for Dependabot/PRs.

**Tradeoff:** CHANGELOG.md is no longer committed into the repo; release notes live in the GitHub Releases. Alternative (not chosen): a bypass PAT to keep the changelog commit.

author: joshkappler
body:
## Summary - add `gt status`: per-locale translation health, fully offline, from the same local sources the translate flow already uses (`collectFiles()`, `createFileMapping()`, `gt-lock.json`, translated files on disk). Prints a coverage table (translated, missing, stale, errors) with no network calls and no API key - validates translated ICU structurally: every entry must parse and keep the source's argument set and kinds through plural/select recursion, using the parser options the runtime formatter uses, so what fails here is what throws in production. That catches the "works in English, crashes in Polish" class `gt validate` cannot see, since it only reads source files - `--ci` exits 1 below `--min-coverage` (default 100), on any validation error, or when nothing was measurable at all; `--verbose` lists every missing and stale unit - honesty guards: composite JSON reports "not measured" rather than counting as covered on file presence, zero measurable units shows a dash and fails `--ci` instead of a fake 100%, and CDN-served gt-next projects get a clear note instead of the config error `collectFiles` would throw ## Testing - TDD throughout: 75 tests across the ICU comparator, catalog diffing, status assembly, table rendering, and CI gating, plus a lockfile round-trip; whole-package suite 2154 passing; `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` clean - built CLI against real fixtures: a JSON + markdown project with a deliberately broken Polish catalog reports the table, all three ICU errors, and both stale units, with `--ci` flipping 1 to 0 after the fix; a gt-react inline project through the real `gt generate` flow reports every breakage with no false ICU errors on JSX tree entries - adversarial probes: a composite-only project, an i18next Russian catalog with `_few`/`_many` (no false stale), a CDN-runtime quickstart, a v1 lockfile orphan ## Notes - prior art: formatjs `verify`, Lingui extract stats, i18n-check. GT had coverage only on the dashboard, so nothing could gate CI and a broken translated ICU string shipped silently until a user hit it - counting units: keys for the GT inline catalog and non-composite JSON, whole files for MD/MDX/YAML; i18next plural families collapse into one unit each, so a CLDR-correct Russian catalog is not flagged - known constraints: right after `gt generate` a self-managed project reads as covered (status counts key presence), YAML counts files not keys, JSX tree entries are not structurally validated yet, and multi-branch v1 lockfiles resolve to the first branch like every other command that reads the lockfile - changeset: gt patch

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `gt status` command that reports per-locale translation coverage (translated, missing, stale, errors) by diffing local source files and translated catalogs against the GT lockfile — entirely offline, with no API key required. A `--ci` flag gates pipelines on coverage and ICU structural validity. - **New `computeStatus` pipeline**: walks `collectFiles`/`aggregateFiles` output, applies `createFileMapping`, and diffs GT-template catalogs, plain JSON (flat-pointer and include-schema), and whole-file formats (MD/YAML) per locale, collapsing i18next plural families to avoid false stale reports. - **ICU structural validator** (`compareMessages.ts`): parses source and translated strings, then checks for missing/extra/mismatched arguments and rich-text tags — catching "works in English, crashes in Polish" failures that `gt validate` cannot see. - **CI gating** (`evaluateStatus`): zero-total locales go to an `unmeasurableLocales` bucket rather than silently counting as 100%, and composite JSON files are explicitly marked as not measured rather than assumed covered.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge — the command is read-only (no writes, no network calls), the CI gate logic is correct, and the test suite is thorough across all five layers of the feature. The change is entirely additive: a new gt status command with no side effects on existing commands or data. The zero-total locale case is correctly binned as unmeasurable rather than silently counted as 100%, the composite-JSON honesty guard is in place, and the ICU argument-set comparator handles plural/select recursion correctly. The only observations are UX gaps — a co-occurring coverage failure can be obscured behind the unmeasurable-locale message, and the ICU parser is invoked with default options that may not perfectly reflect runtime strictness — neither of which affects correctness of the gate or the on-disk state. **Files Needing Attention:** No files require special attention. The status command, diff logic, ICU comparator, and display layer are all well-covered by the accompanying tests.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | packages/cli/src/cli/commands/status.ts | Command entrypoint: handleStatus orchestrates file collection, diffing, display, and CI gating. evaluateStatus correctly bins zero-total locales as unmeasurable rather than covered. Minor UX gap: early return when unmeasurable locales are present suppresses any co-occurring coverage failure message for non-CI users. | | packages/cli/src/translation/status/computeStatus.ts | Core diff logic: correctly handles GT catalog, include/flat JSON, composite JSON (unmeasured), whole-file units, and lockfile orphan stale detection. ICU validation is properly scoped per-key for GT templates and per-file for ICU-format JSON. | | packages/cli/src/formats/icu/compareMessages.ts | ICU argument-set comparator: correctly detects missing/extra/mismatched arguments and rich-text tags through plural/select recursion. Uses default parse() options (no strict mode), which is an acceptable approximation for offline validation. | | packages/cli/src/translation/status/catalogDiff.ts | Key-level diff and i18next plural collapse. Regex correctly covers all CLDR categories plus numeric ordinal suffixes; collapse prevents false stale for CLDR-correct multi-form catalogs. | | packages/cli/src/console/displayStatus.ts | Table renderer: shows dash instead of fake 100% for zero-total rows, caps verbose lists at 25 lines, separates composite-JSON unmeasured note from validation errors. Clean. | | packages/cli/src/formats/json/flattenJson.ts | Adds flattenStringLeaves (RFC 6901 pointer-keyed) and flattenJsonWithStringFilter (JSONPath-based, strings only) used by the status diff. Both implementations are correct; pointer escaping covers ~ and / per spec. | | packages/cli/src/cli/base.ts | Adds setupStatusCommand / handleStatusCommand following existing command patterns; status added to ID_COMPATIBILITY_WARNING_COMMANDS set. |

Flowchart

## Summary

Merge the pinned LeanBitLab/LeanType **v3.9.9** release (`adb7c3755`) into LeanTypeDual without pulling the eight newer `upstream/main` commits that already belong to v4.0.0-beta1.

The update adds system-emoji and app-language settings, multi-row number rows, toolbar swipe-to-dismiss, translation and spellcheck improvements, asynchronous fallback-gesture indexing, dictionary upgrade preservation, and native dictionary crash/ANR fixes. LeanTypeDual's identity, privacy flavors, toolbar/two-thumb features, badges, screenshots, and Fastlane release history remain fork-owned.

Fixes #121.

## Merge decisions

- Kept `com.asafmah.leantypedual`, version `3.10.0` / code `4000`, `compileSdk 36`, and `targetSdk 35`.
- Combined upstream swipe-down dismissal with the fork's toolbar auto-show/hide and hardware-keyboard settings.
- Accepted the upstream fallback-gesture default and translation-language history resolution after auditing Mergiraf output.
- Removed an auto-merged duplicate AndroidX Startup provider while retaining both WorkManager and EmojiCompat initializer removals.
- Excluded LeanBitLab Fastlane changelogs, screenshots, and live badge assets; retained technical upstream release-note documents.

## Reliability fixes found during integration

- Use APK asset `/` paths instead of host `File.separator` for dictionary upgrade/extraction, with red-to-green behavior coverage.
- Preserve upstream's legacy-first direct-IME switching order while making pre-Android-9 no-token paths safe no-ops; SDK-27 and modern direct-switch tests pass.
- Release main-dictionary load waiters in `finally` on failure.
- Make parallel multilingual suggestion workers snapshot-consistent, isolate mutable JNI weight arrays, omit/log failed secondary locales, and always release their latch; failure-path tests prove primary results return instead of hanging.
- Clear file-global InputLogic shadow-handler queues between scenarios to remove full-suite order leakage.

## Verification

- All flavor gates pass: `compileOfflineRunTestsKotlin`, `compileOfflineliteRunTestsKotlin`, `compileStandardRunTestsKotlin`, and `compileStandardfullRunTestsKotlin`.
- Final full Offline debug suite: **294 tests, 11 failed, 1 skipped**; failing names exactly match the `origin/dev` baseline (**284 tests, 11 failed, 1 skipped**). All ten added tests pass.
- Final Offline runTests suite: **294 tests, 4 failed, 1 skipped**; the same four environment-dependent parser failures as the `origin/dev` baseline (**284 tests, 4 failed, 1 skipped**).

- High-effort independent review completed; its missing-final-suite evidence finding was resolved with the post-fix full debug run.
- GitHub Actions `Unit tests` run #29598368167 passes for merge commit `8cc6ebe62`.

## Known test-harness note

The merged full suites can print Robolectric `DefaultDispatcher-worker` teardown warnings without adding test failures. Temporary labeled handlers on both changed dictionary scopes caught no exception, and a RichInputMethodManager diagnostic changed teardown scheduling without reporting a scoped error. No diagnostic handlers are retained.

Draft release PR #120 remains based on pre-v3.9.9 `dev` and separately changes `ImeCompat`, `LatinIME`, and `Suggest`. Merge this PR into `dev` first; then retarget stacked v4.0.2 PR #124 to `dev` and merge it. author: lbliii
body:
Closes #287.

## What changed

- add opt-in `advise_extraction_source()` and `advise_extraction_template()` entry points under `kida.analysis`
- register informational `K-MOD-102` extraction-candidate diagnostics with exact spans, contributing signals, tentative props/slots, dependencies, and related repeated locations
- detect substantial interactive loop regions and normalized repeated interactive siblings while suppressing existing component/block boundaries
- preserve the approved boundary: no `DiagnosticOptions`, `diagnose_source`, CLI/default check, root export, suppression, directory/multi-root, adapter, or rewrite changes
- document the API and error code, add a changelog fragment, a golden machine diagnostic, approved-corpus parity, cache/concurrency proof, and scaling benchmarks

## Why

The shape-profile prerequisite from #288 provides policy-neutral facts, but tooling still needs a conservative single-template advisory layer that can identify likely extraction boundaries without pretending a loop or repetition alone proves a component. This change requires independent structure, interaction/accessibility, and lexical-boundary signals and deliberately emits no safe edit.

## Contract parity

| Contract | API/CLI | Programmatic | Protocol | Schema/Types | Docs | Examples | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Extraction advice | analysis-only exports; no CLI change | `DiagnosticReport` | no adapter/multi-root change | existing immutable `Diagnostic`; new `K-MOD-102` | analysis + errors docs | documented source/template calls | corpus, exact spans, JSON/SARIF, cache, concurrency |

## Steward Notes

- Consulted: analysis, public API, tests, site, and benchmark scoped stewards.
- Risks: source-range accuracy, false positives from loop/branch/size counts, imported component calls becoming props, existing-boundary drift, repeated-sibling scaling, and shared traversal state.
- Evidence: exact-span assertions; all seven approved corpus classifications; imported-call, provide/consume, negative layout/table/tiny-loop/static-repetition cases; fresh/cache-hit and `preserve_ast=False` parity; 64 concurrent calls; golden JSON and SARIF parity.
- Concurrency: parser, HTML structure, dependency indexes, and candidate collections are call-local; returned diagnostics are immutable. No caches, locks, globals, or `ContextVar` behavior changed.
- Render/compiler impact: not applicable; this is an explicit analysis call and does not alter parser ASTs, compilation, caching ABI, escaping, or any render surface.
- Downstream pilot: no-consumer exemption. No deployed consumer currently requests `K-MOD-102`; the approved advisor corpus is the first contract pilot, and multi-root/downstream orchestration remains blocked on #292.
- Unresolved tradeoff: tentative interfaces remain conservative lexical names, not semantic renames; human review is required and no edit is supplied.

## Verification

- `make verify-stability` — 4,791 tests plus coverage gate, lint, format, types, safety/package smoke, and package build passed
- focused analysis/public contract suite — 262 tests passed before final full gate
- `make docs` — 284 pages built; the existing 15 internal-link health findings remain unrelated
- benchmark output sanity passed before timing

author: endazon
body:
## 変更概要

FR-20 段階ゲートの純ドメイン（[IADR-0041](../blob/develop/docs/adr/IADR-0041_stage-gate-transition-logic.md)・PR #98 マージ済み）を**運用系へ結線**する。残スコープであった Application ストア・Worker エンドポイント・DI・EF マイグレーション・遷移履歴の永続化・（Discord）承認フローの結線を実装した。RiskManagementService（`Application`/`Worker`）＋新規 Migration に閉じている（`Shared.Contracts` は不変・他サービス無改修）。

**#16（バックテスト）前提確認**: #16 は CLOSED・Stage 0 合格判定は `BacktestService` に純ドメインとして実装済み。Risk 側の消費点 `StagePerformance.BacktestPassed` は既存。ただし `BacktestService` は Database per Service の別サービスであり verdict の Risk 供給は s2s 統合（本スコープ外）。よって**バックテスト合格の接続は fail-safe な後続フックに留めた**（既定 `BacktestPassed=false`＝Stage 0→1 昇格は既定で拒否。実供給は後続で `IStagePerformanceStore.Save` に流すだけで解錠）。

### 実装内容
- **Application**: `IStageGateStore` / `IStagePerformanceStore` ポート・InMemory アダプタ・`StageGateService`（現状/履歴照会・承認遷移・撤退評価＋自動 kill switch 起動）・`StageGateStatus` DTO
- **Worker 永続化**: `stage_transitions`（追記専用・Sequence 主キー）/ `stage_performance`（単一行）を Risk 専有 DbContext へ追加、`EfStageGateStore` / `EfStagePerformanceStore`、`AddStageGate` マイグレーション
- **Endpoints**: `/risk-controls/stage-gate`（現状）・`/stage-gate/history`（履歴）・`POST /stage-gate/transition`（承認遷移）・`POST /stage-gate/withdrawal/evaluate`（撤退評価＋自動停止）を **owner サブグループ（OwnerOnly）** に追加
- **DI**: ストア（scoped）・`StageGateService`（scoped）・`StageGatePolicy`（singleton＝`TradingDefaults.CreateStagePolicy()` を**参照**）を `Program.cs` の隣接行に配線

## 実装した要求 / ユースケース（トレーサビリティ）

- 機能要求（FR）: **FR-20**（運用段階の管理・段階遷移は利用者承認）／**FR-15**（バックテスト必須ゲート＝fail-safe 接続）
- ユースケース（UC）: **UC-06**（設定・統制の変更・承認）
- 画面（SC）: なし

## 仕様書

- 仕様書: `docs/specs/20260718_20_stage-gate-transitions.md`

## 関連 ADR

- 関連 ADR: **ADR-0008**（段階的実弾投入・撤退基準）／**ADR-0007**（変更は利用者のみ・履歴記録）／ADR-0001（Database per Service）
- 実装 ADR: **IADR-0070**（本 PR の決定）／IADR-0041（純ドメイン）／IADR-0012（Risk EF 永続化）／IADR-0051（OwnerOnly/OwnerOrService）
- ADR 制約からの逸脱: なし

## 計画へのフィードバック

- 計画へのフィードバック: なし（UC-06 が段階遷移承認を明記していない点は #16 の PR #100 で既に注記済み）

## 受け入れ基準のチェック

- [x] 計画書（要求・UC）の受け入れ基準を満たしている
- [x] 基本フロー・代替フロー・例外フローを実装した
- [x] バリデーション（承認者必須・段階整合）を実装した
- [x] 非機能要件（fail-safe・最小権限）に配慮した

### 受け入れ基準 → テストの対応

| 受け入れ基準（骨子） | 対応 |
| --- | --- |
| 承認なしに段階が遷移しない | 承認は `RequestTransition` の唯一経路（空承認拒否）。エンドポイントは OwnerOnly・承認者＝認証済み利用者名。→ 未認証 401／service ロール 403／空承認拒否のテスト |
| 遷移履歴が監査できる | `stage_transitions` 追記専用・`GET /stage-gate/history`。別スコープで読める永続化。→ 永続化・履歴テスト |
| バックテスト合格した戦略のみ Stage 1 へ（fail-safe 既定） | `BacktestPassed` 未記録時 false→Stage 0→1 は 422（`BacktestNotPassed`）。記録後は 200。→ 既定拒否／記録後受理のテスト |
| 差し戻し基準到達時に自動で安全側（停止・降格提案） | `EvaluateWithdrawal` が `HaltNewEntries` 時に kill switch を自動起動、`ProposedStage` を返す。→ 実DD 超で kill switch 起動／既定は非発火のテスト |

## 変更種別

- [x] 新機能（feat）

## チェックリスト

- [x] 着手前に作業仕様書を作成し、それに沿って実装した
- [x] 該当する必須仕様書（作業・データ・テスト）を作成・更新した（作業仕様書 + IADR）
- [x] 重要な実装判断は実装ADR（IADR-0070）に記録した
- [x] ブランチ名・コミットメッセージに起点 ID を含めた
- [x] コード内コメントに起点 ID を残した
- [x] 受け入れ基準・ユースケースのフローをテストに写像した
- [x] ビルド・テストが通っている（全 slnx ビルド 0 警告／Risk: Domain 96・Application 101・Worker 58 緑）
- [x] ADR の確定済み制約に違反していない
- [x] `dotnet format` 準拠
- [x] 秘密情報をコミットしていない

## 後続に切り分けた境界（fail-safe フック）

- **バックテスト verdict / 実DD・統制違反・スリッページ実績の実供給**（`BacktestService` からの s2s・#82 系）: 本 PR は fail-safe 既定（`BacktestPassed=false`）と `IStagePerformanceStore.Save` の受け口までを提供。
- **NotificationService（Discord Bot）側コマンドハンドラ**（`!stage promote/demote` 等）: #15（FR-14）Bot 基盤（`DiscordCommandAuthorizer` → `HttpKillSwitchController` と同型）が本 OwnerOnly エンドポイントを trading-owner マップで呼ぶ薄い追加。NotificationService への変更のため後続に分離（本 PR は Risk 側の呼び出し口を提供）。
- **撤退の定期評価ドライバ**（実 `StagePerformance` を周期供給して `EvaluateWithdrawal` を叩く常駐処理）: 実DD 供給依存のため後続。自動停止の機構は本 PR で完成・単体検証済み。
- **中央監査台帳（FR-11）への `StageTransitioned` バス発行**: 遷移履歴は Risk 専有 DB に永続化・照会可能（＝「監査できる」を充足）。バス発行は `Shared.Contracts` 追加＋Audit Consumer（`AuditConsumerCoverageTests`）を伴うため本 PR では追加せず後続に分離。

## レビュアーへの補足

- 受け入れ基準は充足だが、バックテスト verdict の**実供給**（s2s）を後続に分離したため `Closes` ではなく **`Refs #20`** とした（境界は IADR-0070・仕様書に明記）。
- **IADR 番号**: 0069 は #18 が確保する想定のため 0070 を採番（着手時に全ブランチを走査し 0068 のみ使用中を確認）。README は 0070 の 1 行のみ昇順追記。
- **並行注意**: 本 PR は RiskManagementService＋新規 Migration に閉じ、`Shared.Contracts` 無改修・Risk `Program.cs` の DI は隣接行に限定。#18 と交差しない。

Refs #20

body:
## Summary

Fixes **BB-63**: after BB-45 added the split-pane maximize/restore control, its double-arrow glyphs read oversized and off-rhythm next to the close (×) and right-panel controls.

Diagnosis (measured, not eyeballed): all three controls already share the same sanctioned button box (`HEADER_ICON_BUTTON_CLASS`, 28×28 / 16px glyph) and are geometrically centered — no baseline error. The maximize/restore glyphs (`ArrowExpand01`/`ArrowShrink01`) simply paint to ~66% of the 24px icon grid vs the compact close (~32%), so at the shared 16px size they dwarf the close beside them. Every other surface that renders these glyphs already reduces them (prompt box 12px, panel-collapse 14px) — the pane header was the lone 16px outlier.

## Change

- Add a shared sanctioned reduced-glyph header-button class (`COARSE_POINTER_HEADER_REDUCED_GLYPH_ICON_BUTTON_CLASS`, surfaced in-app as `HEADER_MAXIMIZE_ICON_BUTTON_CLASS`) that reuses the **exact** standard button box and only paints the glyph one optical step smaller: **13px fine / 16px coarse** (measured as the point where its footprint matches the close).
- The 28/36px button box — and thus the pointer/focus hit target — is unchanged. Close and right-panel controls are untouched.
- Refactored the box geometry into a shared constant so the standard and reduced variants can't drift; kept the vendored `apps/web` copy in sync and regenerated the plugin-registry / templates outputs.

No colors touched (glyph uses `currentColor`, palette-invariant). No server↔host-daemon contract change, so `HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is intentionally unchanged.

## Validation

- New geometry-contract test (`headerIconButtonSizing.test.ts`) + `PaneMaximizeButton` — 7 passed. App thread-detail + layout suites — 21 files / 128 passed.
- Typecheck: app, shared-ui, web, plugin-registry, templates. Build: app, shared-ui. Plugin-registry `--check` regenerated & up to date.
- Real-product QA (isolated build, **web + Electron @ DPR 2×**): 2-pane, nested 4-pane (all maximize 13px), maximized/restored, right panel open/closed, narrow (900px), light + dark + Nord custom palette, tooltip + `⌘⇧E` toggle + focus-visible ring (wraps full 28px box), and live `bb thread pane maximize`/`restore` CLI paths.

## Independent review

One readonly codex `gpt-5.6-sol` (medium) review on the MacBook Pro checkout returned **APPROVE** with no findings (confirmed box/hit-target preserved, Tailwind + generated CSS resolve correctly, all copies synchronized, no wire change). No second review requested.

author: yurmil
body:
Closes #7.

Moves tube-point layout generation off the main thread into a dedicated Web Worker, so a layout is computed without competing with rendering.

## Changes
- **`core/layout-strategies`**: extracted shared `computeLayoutPoints(params)` (strategy points + cutoff filter), used by both the worker and the fallback.
- **`layout-worker` + `layout-worker-client`**: compute points in a worker and transfer them back as an interleaved `Float64Array` buffer (cheap for large layouts). The client recreates the worker after a crash and **falls back to a synchronous compute** if a worker can't be created or errors — the app never loses layout.
- **`useGeneratorState`**: `tubeCoords` is now async state, requested on each deferred params change with latest-wins stale-response handling. The initial layout is seeded synchronously to avoid a first-paint flash.
- `MAX_TUBE_POINTS` stays as a render/interaction guard (canvas + RBush are still main-thread); comment updated.

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅ · `pnpm test` (58, incl. new codec round-trip tests) ✅ · `pnpm build` ✅
- In-browser: worker actually instantiated (`layout-worker.ts?worker_file` request), initial 169 holes seeded, pitch→40 recomputes to 109 asynchronously, click-select/hit-test works against worker-provided points, no error boundary.
